parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and periodically update access control policy and procedures for systems that store, process, or transfer model weights. Address responsibilities for organization-defined personnel or roles, relevant environments including build pipelines, training infrastructure, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems, and coordination with enterprise access control processes. Designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of these policies. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as security incidents, changes to model weight handling practices, or material changes to the training or serving infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish account management processes for model weight environments that define permitted and prohibited account types, approval and provisioning requirements, role-appropriate access criteria, monitoring, and timely modification or removal of access when personnel or business need changes. Prohibit shared, anonymous, and group-owned accounts for direct model weight access; where service accounts are required for automated pipelines or inference serving, provision them with unique credentials scoped to the minimum access needed. Require explicit authorization and documented justification for accounts that access weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, or serving infrastructure, with approvals from organization-defined personnel before access is granted. Specify for each account the authorized user or service, group and role membership, and the access privileges granted, including whether access is read-only or read-write and whether it extends to production weights. Monitor account activity for access pattern anomalies, including unexpected volume, off-hours access, or access inconsistent with assigned role, and generate alerts through normal security operations processes. Establish processes to promptly modify or revoke access when personnel are terminated, transferred, or change roles, and to detect and act on changes in business need before the next scheduled review. Review all accounts with access to model weight environments at an organization-defined, risk-based frequency, with privileged and production weight access reviewed more frequently than general access. Use additional controls for accounts with access to the most sensitive weight assets, including production checkpoints and pre-release models.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use automated mechanisms to support provisioning, modification, review, and removal of accounts for model weight systems. Automate role-based access where feasible, distinguish at least between read and read-write access to model weights, and automate attestation or recertification for ongoing access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automatically disable temporary and emergency accounts used to access model weight systems after an organization-defined period appropriate to each account type and associated risk. For emergency accounts used to access production weights or weight-serving infrastructure, generate a security alert upon activation and require a documented review after the account is disabled. Apply shorter expiration windows to accounts with write or export access to model weights than to read-only access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automatically disable temporary model weight access accounts after an organization-defined period. Disable accounts that are expired, inactive beyond an organization-defined period, no longer associated with a user or role, or otherwise inconsistent with policy or risk decisions. Coordinate disablement with existing personnel and account management processes, and review dormant accounts periodically.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automatically record account lifecycle actions affecting model weight systems and protect those records with separate access controls. Alert on account changes that materially increase risk, such as emergency access activation, unusual bulk changes, or suspicious sequences linking account changes to sensitive weight access attempts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require users to log out of interactive sessions when prolonged inactivity is expected, and enforce workstation or console locking for systems used to access model weights. For long-running research workflows such as training runs or checkpoint monitoring, use reauthentication and session management controls that fit operational needs instead of aggressively terminating noninteractive work.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use separate privileged accounts for administering systems that store or process model weights, distinct from standard user accounts where feasible. Define and document privileged roles, apply additional controls to privileged use, and establish policy governing privileged actions taken by automation or AI agents. Use managed administrative environments or equivalent safeguards commensurate with risk. Monitor privileged role assignments and changes to those assignments, and revoke privileged access when the underlying business need or role justification no longer applies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit shared or group accounts for access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. For service accounts that access weights programmatically, require unique credentials per service and use certificate-based or equivalent strong authentication. Maintain a registry of all service accounts with weight access, documenting owner, purpose, and access scope, and rotate service account credentials on an organization-defined, risk-based schedule.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitor model weight accounts for atypical usage using logging and anomaly detection appropriate to the environment. Focus on changes in access pattern, location, volume, concurrency, or role alignment that may indicate misuse, and generate alerts through normal security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Disable or restrict model weight access for individuals when credible risk indicators, investigations, or personnel actions justify doing so under organizational policy and applicable law. Use a documented review process, avoid automatic triggers that are not clearly risk-based, and monitor for unauthorized reactivation attempts. Require documented authorization through an organization-defined review process before restoring access to model weight systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce access control policies for all systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference infrastructure. Deny access by default and require explicit authorization for each role or principal. Separate access permissions across distinct asset classes, model weights, architecture definitions, training data, and configuration artifacts, so that access to one does not imply or enable access to another. Implement technical controls that prevent unauthorized export or exfiltration of weights, ensuring that the ability to read weights within an authorized training or serving context does not automatically confer the ability to copy or transfer them externally without additional authorization. Log all access attempts, successful and failed, with sufficient attribution to support investigation and accountability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Apply least privilege to model weight systems by limiting direct access to the minimum needed for job responsibilities, separating read and read-write access where appropriate, and using time-limited elevation for temporary access only for the minimum time required. Maintain emergency access processes with additional oversight.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Explicitly authorize access to security-relevant functions that protect model weights, including key management, access control systems, audit pipelines, network controls, and cluster administration systems. Limit such access to organization-defined personnel or roles, document authorized assignments, and review them at an organization-defined, risk-based frequency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require users with privileged access to model weight systems to use separate, unprivileged accounts for routine activities such as email, web browsing, document editing, and collaboration tools. Enforce technical controls that prevent privileged weight access accounts from initiating outbound internet connections, accessing external communication services, or mounting removable media during active weight access sessions. Apply these restrictions at the platform or operating system level so they cannot be bypassed by end-user action.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Limit privileged accounts to a documented minimal set of roles requiring administrative access to infrastructure that stores, processes, or protects model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Provision and remove such access through role-based automation or controlled workflows, and review privileged roles and assignments periodically to confirm each account remains justified by current operational responsibilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Review model weight access roles and privileged assignments at an organization-defined, risk-based frequency, with emphasis on the roles that automatically grant weight access. Remove or adjust access that is no longer justified by current responsibilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Log privileged actions affecting model weights and the systems that protect them, including weight file operations, encryption key access, checkpoint exports, weight transfers between storage tiers, access control modifications, and security configuration changes. Capture sufficient detail to support investigation and accountability, including user identity, target weight artifact, operation type, and outcome. Centralize or forward those logs to a protected logging environment with access controls separate from the systems being logged, and without requiring unnecessarily precise timing or unrealistic delivery latencies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Implement technical controls preventing non-privileged accounts from executing privileged operations on model weight infrastructure, including encryption key access, access control modifications, weight file deletion, weight export to external systems, and security configuration changes. Use operating system-level mandatory access controls enforcing weight file access restrictions based on least-privilege policy, and apply kernel or hypervisor-level hardening to reduce the attack surface for privilege escalation on systems that store, process, or serve model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce limits on consecutive failed authentication attempts for all access points to model weight infrastructure, including interactive consoles, APIs, SSH endpoints, and management interfaces. When the organization-defined threshold is exceeded, automatically lock the account or session and require either a timed delay before retry or administrative release, based on account type and risk level. Apply stricter lockout behavior to privileged accounts and service accounts with access to weight repositories, training clusters, or inference serving systems than to standard user accounts. Generate security alerts when failed attempt patterns suggest credential stuffing, brute force, or targeted access attempts against weight storage or serving endpoints. Review and tune thresholds periodically to balance security against operational disruption from legitimate access failures in automated training and inference pipelines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose:
Establish and enforce documented remote access policies for all systems that store, process, or serve model weights, covering permitted access types, required authentication methods, session controls, and conditions under which remote access is authorized or denied. Authorize each remote access type prior to permitting connections, and review authorizations periodically or when access needs change.

Require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to model weight environments, using phishing-resistant methods where technically feasible. Prohibit direct remote access to weight storage and training infrastructure; route all administrative remote connections through monitored jump hosts or equivalent access control points with session logging enabled. Enforce full-tunnel routing for remote connections to model weight systems to prevent traffic from bypassing monitoring controls.

Restrict remote access to organization-approved devices meeting defined security posture requirements, and prohibit access from unmanaged or personal devices to systems holding production or sensitive model weights. Configure remote sessions to terminate or require reauthentication after an organization-defined period of inactivity appropriate to the sensitivity of the accessed environment. Log all remote sessions accessing model weight systems with sufficient detail to support investigation, and alert on activity indicative of bulk weight exfiltration or anomalous transfer volumes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Employ automated mechanisms to monitor and control remote access to model weight systems, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure. Capture sufficient session detail to support detection and investigation, including connection origin, session duration, data volumes transferred, and actions taken on weight files or related credentials. Generate alerts on remote access activity that materially elevates risk, such as large-volume weight downloads, access to cryptographic keys or signing credentials, privilege escalation, and access from locations or at times inconsistent with established patterns. Integrate remote access monitoring with centralized logging and security operations processes so that anomalous sessions can be investigated and terminated promptly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce strong encryption for all remote access sessions to systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference infrastructure. Prohibit unencrypted or weakly encrypted remote access protocols and require current, well-supported cryptographic standards for both confidentiality and integrity protection. Apply equivalent encryption requirements to automated or service-to-service remote connections, such as those used by build pipelines, orchestration systems, or distributed training jobs accessing weights remotely. Review and update cryptographic configurations periodically to retire deprecated algorithms or protocol versions as guidance and threat conditions evolve.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Route all remote access to model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems, through organization-defined managed access control points. Prohibit direct remote connections to weight storage or processing systems that bypass these control points. Enforce this routing through network-layer controls, not solely through policy, and ensure managed access points provide sufficient logging to support session attribution and investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict remote execution of privileged operations affecting model weights, including weight copying, bulk export, encryption key access, access control modifications, and checkpoint deletion, to explicitly authorized use cases documented with a business or operational justification. Require multi-party authorization for remote privileged weight operations, with approvers drawn from organization-defined roles that are independent of the requester. Log all remote privileged commands with sufficient session detail to support forensic review, and generate real-time alerts to security operations personnel upon execution. Prohibit remote privileged weight access through general-purpose remote desktop or collaboration tools; require purpose-built, hardened access paths with strong authentication and session integrity controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit wireless network interfaces on systems that directly store, serve, or process model weights; disable or physically remove wireless hardware where technically feasible. Where wireless connectivity to model weight development or training environments is operationally necessary, authorize it explicitly, enforce strong mutual authentication and encryption, and restrict wireless networks from routing to model weight storage and serving infrastructure through network segmentation. Conduct periodic wireless surveys of facilities housing model weight systems to detect unauthorized or rogue access points, and investigate anomalies through normal security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit mobile devices from directly accessing model weight storage, training clusters, and inference serving infrastructure. Where mobile access to development or operational platforms is operationally justified, require enrollment in a managed device program that enforces full-device encryption, containerization of work-related data, screen locking, and current OS patching. Authorize mobile device connections to model weight environments through an explicit approval process, and enforce technical controls at the application and API layers to prevent model weight downloads or transfers to mobile devices. Enable and periodically test remote wipe capability for enrolled devices with access to model weight environments. Monitor for and block access from devices that fail to meet security baselines or show signs of compromise.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate awareness and training policy and procedures for personnel who store, access, train, fine-tune, serve, or otherwise handle model weights. The policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, and coordination across relevant environments including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, and inference infrastructure. Update policy and procedures following significant changes to the model weight environment, weight-related security incidents, or shifts in the threat landscape affecting AI assets. Assign responsibility for maintaining and disseminating the policy to organization-defined personnel or roles, and review both policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deliver security literacy training to all personnel with access to model weight systems, covering threats specific to AI/ML environments such as social engineering targeting weight credentials, unsafe model checkpoint handling, secure use of training and inference infrastructure, and incident reporting obligations. Provide training during onboarding and at an organization-defined recurring frequency. Update training content at an organization-defined frequency and following model weight security incidents, significant changes to weight storage or serving infrastructure, or emerging threat activity relevant to AI/ML environments. Incorporate lessons learned from internal incidents and relevant external events into updated content. Supplement formal training with awareness techniques appropriate to the environment, such as targeted advisories on active threats to model weight systems, simulated attacks against weight access credentials, or periodic communications reinforcing secure handling of checkpoints and training artifacts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Train all personnel with access to model weight environments to recognize and report potential insider threat indicators relevant to AI intellectual property, including access to weights outside an individual's normal role or project scope, unusual volume or pattern of weight downloads or exports, attempts to move weights to unauthorized destinations, and efforts to circumvent access controls or audit mechanisms. Provide a confidential, accessible reporting channel for weight-related security concerns. Refresh this training at an organization-defined frequency and incorporate representative examples drawn from weight theft or exfiltration scenarios appropriate to the organization's environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Train authorized personnel with access to model weights, weight repositories, training infrastructure, and serving systems to recognize and report social engineering tactics likely to target AI intellectual property. Instruction must cover credential phishing targeting weight system access, pretexting to extract information about weight storage locations or access procedures, and solicitation or recruitment attempts aimed at obtaining model weights or insider knowledge. Provide clear, accessible reporting channels for personnel to flag suspicious contacts or attempts, and reinforce reporting expectations as part of ongoing awareness activities at an organization-defined frequency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Train personnel with access to model weight systems to recognize and report indicators of compromise relevant to weight storage, training, and serving environments. Training must cover behaviors such as unexpected or unauthorized access attempts to weight repositories, anomalous process activity in training clusters or inference servers, unusual data movement patterns involving weight files or checkpoints, and system performance anomalies during weight loading or serving operations that may indicate tampering or exfiltration. Establish and communicate clear reporting procedures so personnel can escalate suspected anomalies to security operations through a consistent, low-friction path. Deliver training at onboarding and refresh it at an organization-defined frequency, with targeted updates when new threat patterns relevant to model weight environments are identified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Train authorized personnel with access to model weight systems on threat actor tactics relevant to AI intellectual property theft, including long-term credential harvesting, lateral movement toward weight repositories and training infrastructure, living-off-the-land techniques that abuse legitimate tooling, and slow or staged exfiltration designed to evade detection thresholds. Incorporate current threat intelligence on campaigns targeting AI organizations and model weight assets into recurring awareness activities. Supplement training with periodic exercises that simulate realistic weight theft scenarios, testing detection, response, and coordination across teams responsible for weight storage, training pipelines, and serving infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Provide ongoing security awareness training to personnel with access to model weight systems that reflects the current threat environment facing AI development organizations. Include training content addressing threats relevant to model weight security: adversarial attempts to exfiltrate weights or checkpoints, supply chain risks in training pipelines and dependency management, model extraction and reconstruction techniques, and insider threat indicators specific to AI development environments. Update training content as the threat landscape evolves, incorporating recent incidents, newly observed attack patterns, and changes to the organization's own weight infrastructure. Tailor content to reflect the access and responsibilities of different personnel, those involved in training, fine-tuning, serving, or storing weights face meaningfully different threat exposures, without requiring separate formal programs for each role.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deliver role-based security training to authorized personnel before granting access to model weight systems and at an organization-defined frequency thereafter. Tailor training content to each role's actual access and responsibilities, personnel who administer weight storage, training clusters, build pipelines, or inference serving infrastructure should receive training specific to those environments, covering topics such as secure handling of model checkpoints, risks associated with ML framework supply chains, insider threat indicators, proper use of access controls and audit mechanisms, and expected behavior during incidents involving model weight exposure or exfiltration. Update training content at an organization-defined frequency and in response to significant changes to weight management infrastructure, tooling, or access policies. Incorporate lessons learned from internal incidents and relevant external events involving model weight theft, unauthorized access, or pipeline compromise into updated training material.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate audit and accountability policy and procedures covering all systems and pipelines that store, process, transfer, or serve model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference infrastructure. Policy must address the purpose and scope of logging requirements across these environments, roles and responsibilities for log collection and oversight, management commitment, and coordination between security operations and teams responsible for model weight systems. Procedures must address how audit logging is implemented, collected, retained, analyzed, and used to support investigation of weight access anomalies or incidents. Designate an organization-defined official responsible for maintaining and disseminating policy and procedures. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as security incidents, material changes to weight infrastructure, or identified gaps in audit coverage.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify the categories of events that model weight systems are capable of logging, including authentication and authorization events on weight repositories and training infrastructure, access to and transfer of weight files and checkpoints, privilege escalation and administrative actions affecting weight storage or serving systems, configuration changes to training clusters and inference infrastructure, deployment and promotion of model weights across environments, and anomalous or bulk data movement involving weight artifacts. Coordinate event selection with security operations and other organizational functions that rely on audit data to ensure logged events collectively support detection, investigation, and after-the-fact analysis of incidents involving model weight compromise or exfiltration. Specify which event types are actively logged, under what conditions or at what frequency, and document a rationale explaining why the selected events are sufficient to support incident investigation. Review and update the selected event types at an organization-defined frequency and whenever significant changes occur to weight storage, training pipelines, or serving infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure that audit records generated by model weight systems contain sufficient detail to support investigation, attribution, and reconstruction of events. At minimum, records must capture the type of operation performed, the time at which it occurred, the system or component where it occurred, the identity of the user or service account responsible, the specific model weight artifact affected (such as a file path, model identifier, or checkpoint version), and the outcome of the event. For programmatic or automated access, including training jobs, fine-tuning pipelines, and inference serving, include additional context that links the action to its originating process or workflow, such as a job or request identifier. Calibrate the granularity of records to support forensic reconstruction of significant events, including bulk access, exfiltration attempts, or unauthorized modification of weights, without imposing logging overhead that degrades operational performance.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enhance audit records for model weight access and operations to include fields that meaningfully support investigation and accountability in weight environments. At minimum, capture the identity of the weight artifact involved (such as checkpoint identifier or model version), the type of operation performed, the volume of data accessed or transferred, source and destination systems or endpoints, the authenticated identity and role context of the requester, and the associated job or workflow (such as training run, fine-tuning job, or inference request) where determinable. Include the authentication method used for the session. Where operationally feasible, include cryptographic hash or integrity metadata for the accessed weight artifact to support post-incident verification. Supplement individual event records with sufficient contextual signals, such as concurrent privileged operations or recent authentication events, to allow correlation across related activity without requiring exhaustive collection of every possible field.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Allocate audit log storage capacity sufficient to retain model weight access logs for an organization-defined retention period without loss or truncation. Monitor storage utilization continuously and generate alerts before capacity limits are reached, allowing time for remediation or archival before log loss occurs. Implement automated archival to secondary or long-term storage for logs covering weight repositories, training clusters, inference infrastructure, and build pipelines, prioritizing retention of logs that would support investigation of insider threat activity or exfiltration of high-value weights. Calibrate retention periods to the realistic timescales of threats relevant to the organization's model weight environment, recognizing that sophisticated insider campaigns may not surface for extended periods after initial access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Detect and alert on audit logging failures affecting model weight systems, including failures in log generation, forwarding, storage, or integrity verification. Route alerts to organization-defined personnel through reliable channels that do not depend on the failing logging infrastructure. For high-sensitivity weight operations, such as weight export, deletion, bulk download, or access to encryption keys protecting weights, require functional audit logging as a precondition and block or defer the operation if logging cannot be confirmed. Maintain redundant log destinations so that a failure at any single destination does not result in a gap in the audit record for weight access and modification events. Upon detecting a logging failure, initiate investigation and preserve any partial records already captured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Review and analyze audit records from model weight systems, including repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, build pipelines, and inference servers, at a frequency appropriate to the sensitivity and access volume of each environment. Focus analysis on indicators relevant to model weight exfiltration, unauthorized access, and insider misuse: access patterns inconsistent with role or historical behavior, bulk or sequential reads of weight files, transfers to external destinations, access outside normal working patterns, failed authentication followed by successful access, and concurrent sessions from disparate locations or systems. Use automated behavioral analysis to detect anomalies at a scale and speed that manual review cannot sustain. Report findings to organization-defined security personnel or roles through established escalation processes, with urgency proportionate to the assessed risk. Adjust the depth, frequency, and focus of review when credible threat information, personnel risk indicators, ongoing investigations, or changes in the operational environment indicate elevated risk to model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use consistent, authoritative time sources across all systems involved in storing, training, fine-tuning, and serving model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Record timestamps in audit logs at a granularity sufficient to support forensic correlation across distributed components, fine enough to reconstruct event sequences during incident investigation. Express timestamps in a consistent, unambiguous format using a standard time reference, with any local offset clearly recorded. Monitor for time synchronization failures across model weight infrastructure and treat persistent or unexplained clock drift as a potential indicator of tampering or evasion activity warranting investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protect audit logs covering model weight access, training runs, checkpoint operations, and serving activity against unauthorized access, modification, and deletion. Use technical controls that prevent log tampering, including immutable or append-only storage for weight-related audit records, with write access restricted independently from the systems being audited. Ensure that administrative access to model weight infrastructure does not confer the ability to alter or delete the audit records generated by that infrastructure. Store audit logs in a system with authentication and access controls separate from the weight repositories, training clusters, and inference environments they cover. Back up audit records to an independent location to protect against loss or destruction. Alert organization-defined personnel when unauthorized access to, modification of, or deletion of model weight audit records is detected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict management of audit logging functionality for model weight systems, including configuration of log sources, modification of retention settings, and deletion or purging of records, to a dedicated, organization-defined subset of privileged personnel that is operationally separate from those who administer training clusters, weight repositories, inference serving infrastructure, and build pipelines. Enforce this separation through technical access controls rather than policy alone, ensuring that administrators of model weight systems cannot alter or suppress the audit trail of their own actions. Implement immutable or append-only storage for weight access and administrative audit logs so that records cannot be modified or deleted even by personnel with privileged access to the logging infrastructure itself.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and periodically update policy and procedures for the security assessment, authorization, and monitoring of systems that store, process, or transfer model weights. Address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant environments including training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference serving infrastructure. Disseminate policy and procedures to organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for model weight security, and designate an organization-defined official to oversee their development and ongoing maintenance. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as security assessments, incidents, or material changes to model weight infrastructure or the threat environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain formal agreements governing all exchanges of model weights, training checkpoints, or weight-derived artifacts between internal systems and external or third-party environments. For each exchange relationship, including cloud training infrastructure, inference hosting providers, fine-tuning partners, and research collaborators, document the interface characteristics, the classification and sensitivity of the weights being exchanged, encryption and access control requirements in transit and at rest, and the responsibilities of each party for protecting the weights. Require that agreements address conditions under which weights may be copied, retained, or further shared, and include explicit provisions for breach notification and weight destruction or return at the end of the relationship. Review and update agreements at an organization-defined frequency and whenever the exchange relationship, system architecture, weight sensitivity, or participating parties materially change.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify transitive data flows involving model weight systems, including downstream systems that receive, cache, forward, or otherwise handle weights as a result of direct exchanges, and document those pathways as part of the organization's model weight access inventory. When the security posture of a downstream system in a transitive exchange cannot be verified, take active steps to suspend or restrict that exchange until verification is restored, preventing indirect exfiltration or unauthorized redistribution of weights through intermediary systems such as shared pipelines, federated training infrastructure, inference proxies, or external partner environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Designate a senior official as the authorizing official responsible for systems that store, process, transmit, or otherwise handle model weights, including weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Before authorizing such systems to operate, the authorizing official must review the implemented security controls, accept any inherited common controls relevant to the weight environment, and explicitly accept the residual risk associated with operating the system given the current control posture. For systems that provide common controls inherited by model weight environments, designate an authorizing official responsible for those controls and for approving their use by inheriting systems. Update authorizations at an organization-defined frequency and when significant changes occur, such as major architecture changes to weight infrastructure, changes in the threat environment, or findings from security assessments that materially affect the risk posture. Base ongoing authorization decisions on evidence from continuous monitoring programs where available, rather than on point-in-time assessments alone.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a continuous monitoring program for infrastructure that stores, trains, serves, or otherwise handles model weights. Define metrics relevant to model weight security, including weight repository access patterns, authentication failures, data transfer volumes and destinations, configuration changes to training clusters and inference systems, and the status of key protective controls such as encryption, integrity verification, and access enforcement. Conduct monitoring and control effectiveness assessments at organization-defined frequencies appropriate to the risk profile of each environment, with more sensitive environments such as production weight repositories and training clusters assessed more frequently than lower-risk systems. Correlate access logs, pipeline activity, and infrastructure events to detect anomalies such as unusual bulk weight reads, unexpected export or replication of checkpoint files, access outside normal operational patterns, or changes to controls that protect weights. Analyze correlated findings, investigate significant anomalies, and take documented response actions when monitoring reveals potential compromise, control degradation, or policy violation. Report the security status of model weight environments to organization-defined personnel at a frequency appropriate to operational tempo, and ensure that monitoring outputs feed into broader security operations and incident response processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Integrate risk monitoring into the continuous monitoring strategy for model weight environments, covering three dimensions: effectiveness monitoring of controls protecting weight storage, training, and serving infrastructure; compliance monitoring for access, handling, and transfer policies governing model weights; and change monitoring for modifications to weight repositories, training pipelines, inference systems, and the security controls that protect them. Collect and correlate signals across these dimensions, including access anomalies, control degradation, configuration drift, and relevant external threat intelligence, to maintain a current understanding of risk to model weight confidentiality and integrity. Surface material changes in risk posture through organization-defined reporting and escalation processes, and use findings to drive timely adjustments to controls or monitoring coverage.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct penetration testing of model weight infrastructure at an organization-defined frequency, with test scenarios calibrated to realistic OC3-level threats including insider exfiltration of weights, credential compromise of accounts with weight access, supply chain attacks targeting ML frameworks or build pipelines, and API-based model extraction through inference endpoints. Test the effectiveness of access controls, encryption, network segmentation, data loss prevention, and detection and alerting capabilities across weight repositories, training clusters, and serving infrastructure. Engage testers with demonstrated knowledge of model weight attack techniques and AI/ML system architectures. Remediate identified vulnerabilities according to a risk-based prioritization process, with critical findings addressed on an expedited basis. Document test scope, findings, and remediation status, and use results to inform ongoing security improvements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require penetration testing of model weight systems to be performed by an independent team or agent with no operational responsibility for the systems under test. Scope testing to weight-specific attack surfaces including access control bypass, credential abuse, weight exfiltration via APIs or bulk storage interfaces, pipeline compromise, and insider threat simulation. Provide testers with sufficient system context, including architecture, access control configuration, and network topology, to enable realistic, targeted testing rather than generic external assessment. Track findings to remediation and use results to inform risk decisions about model weight controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct red team exercises that simulate adversary attempts to compromise model weight confidentiality and integrity, including scenarios tailored to the specific threat profile of weight repositories, training infrastructure, build pipelines, and inference serving systems. Exercises should include at minimum one scenario in which a participant holds legitimate access to model weights, reflecting the insider threat risk inherent to environments where authorized personnel routinely handle high-value weight artifacts. Define rules of engagement and success criteria before each exercise, including what constitutes a meaningful exfiltration or integrity violation of model weights. Evaluate detection capability, response effectiveness, and the degree to which controls prevented or delayed unauthorized weight access or removal. Document findings, track remediation of identified gaps, and use results to inform control improvements across the weight lifecycle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct physical penetration testing of facilities housing model weight infrastructure at an organization-defined frequency, using unannounced attempts where operationally feasible to avoid forewarning defenders. Testing must cover physical access controls protecting weight storage and compute areas, including badge and credential bypass attempts, tailgating through controlled entry points, and unauthorized introduction of devices capable of exfiltrating or tampering with weight storage media. Include scenarios targeting after-hours access and insider-assisted physical compromise, where authorized personnel attempt to access systems or areas beyond their sanctioned scope. Document identified physical security gaps, assign remediation ownership, and track findings to closure within an organization-defined timeframe commensurate with severity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and maintain configuration management policy and procedures covering systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference infrastructure. Policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, coordination across organizational teams, and compliance expectations. Procedures must support consistent implementation of configuration management practices across model weight environments. Assign ownership of policy and procedure development, documentation, and dissemination to organization-defined personnel or roles. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to model weight infrastructure, security incidents affecting weight systems, or material shifts in organizational risk posture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain documented baseline configurations for all infrastructure used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, GPU nodes, inference servers, checkpoint storage systems, and build pipeline components. Baseline configurations must reflect a hardened, minimal-service posture appropriate to each component's role in the model weight lifecycle, covering OS configuration, enabled services, storage encryption, network segmentation, and approved software components including ML frameworks and libraries with verified provenance. Maintain baselines under configuration control so that deviations are detectable and unauthorized changes are not silently accepted. Review and update baselines when components are installed or upgraded, when security-relevant changes are made to weight infrastructure, or when organization-defined circumstances, such as a security incident or significant architecture change, indicate that the current baseline no longer reflects an acceptable posture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Retain an organization-defined number of previous versions of baseline configurations for systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including access control policies, encryption settings, network segmentation rules, and audit configurations. Store configuration backups in immutable storage that is logically or physically separate from production weight systems, and maintain cryptographic hashes of each retained version to support integrity verification. Retain configurations across a time window sufficient to support meaningful rollback; account for the pace of configuration change in the environment, ensuring that retained versions span enough elapsed time to be useful rather than representing only a narrow recent window. Test rollback procedures at an organization-defined frequency to confirm that configurations can be reliably restored and that restored configurations do not inadvertently expose model weights or degrade security controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit devices with direct access to model weights from travel to high-risk locations where the risk of compromise, coercion, or seizure is elevated. Where travel is operationally essential, issue dedicated travel devices provisioned without model weight access and configured with encrypted storage, remote wipe capability, and minimal software footprint. Upon return, quarantine travel devices and conduct a security review for evidence of tampering or unauthorized access before permitting reconnection to any model weight infrastructure. Establish a documented return process that includes personnel debriefing and log review for any anomalous activity associated with accounts used during travel.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and enforce a configuration change control process for all infrastructure that stores, trains, fine-tunes, or serves model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Define the categories of changes subject to configuration control, such as modifications to access controls, encryption configurations, network boundaries, ML framework versions, serving stacks, and storage backends, and document the security and integrity impact of proposed changes on model weight confidentiality, availability, and provenance before approval. Require review and explicit approval of configuration-controlled changes through an organization-defined review process with security representation, and prohibit implementation of unapproved changes to weight-handling infrastructure. Record change decisions, approvals, and outcomes, and retain those records for an organization-defined period sufficient to support security investigations and audits. Monitor the implementation of approved changes to verify they were applied as authorized, and detect unauthorized or undocumented modifications to weight-handling systems through comparison against known-good configuration baselines. Coordinate change control oversight at an organization-defined frequency or when triggered by conditions such as significant architecture changes, security incidents, or new weight deployment pipelines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use automated mechanisms to manage configuration changes across model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Automatically document proposed changes to security-relevant configurations such as weight access policies, encryption settings, network segmentation, and audit pipelines. Route proposed changes to organization-defined approvers and block implementation until required approvals are received. Flag changes that remain pending approval beyond an organization-defined period for escalation or disposition. Record all completed changes with sufficient detail to support accountability and rollback, and notify organization-defined personnel when approved changes are implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test and validate all configuration changes to model weight storage, training infrastructure, serving systems, and protective controls in an environment that reflects production conditions before deploying those changes to production. Verify that changes preserve expected behavior for access controls, encryption of weights at rest and in transit, network segmentation, and audit logging. Document test results, any security-relevant deviations observed, and a security impact assessment for each change. Require sign-off from organization-defined authorized personnel confirming that confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements for model weights are maintained before promoting changes to production.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Analyze the security impact of proposed changes to model weight infrastructure, pipelines, and protection controls before implementation. Scope analysis to cover changes to training clusters, weight repositories, inference serving systems, build and deployment pipelines, ML frameworks and dependencies, access control configurations, and encryption or key management settings. Assess effects on weight confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and identify whether the change weakens any existing protection control. Require documented review and approval by organization-defined roles before applying changes that materially affect weight protection, and use the analysis to inform rollback planning and post-change monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: After changes to model weight storage, training infrastructure, build pipelines, or serving systems, verify that security controls protecting model weights continue to operate as intended. Verification should cover access restrictions on weight repositories, encryption of weights at rest and in transit, network segmentation isolating weight infrastructure, and audit logging of weight access and movement. Tailor the scope and depth of verification to the nature and risk of the change, a configuration update to a serving cluster warrants targeted re-validation of affected controls, while a major infrastructure change or migration warrants broader verification across the weight protection stack. Document verification outcomes and resolve identified gaps before treating the change as complete.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce logical and physical access restrictions on changes to model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, build pipelines, and inference serving systems. Restrict the ability to initiate, approve, and implement changes to organization-defined roles, ensuring that individuals who request changes to sensitive components cannot also approve or execute them without independent authorization. Apply elevated change controls to modifications affecting access control configurations, encryption of weight storage or transit, network segmentation, audit pipelines, and integrity verification mechanisms. Require multi-party approval for changes to these security-relevant components, with approvers drawn from roles independent of the requestor. Enforce these restrictions through technical controls in change management workflows rather than relying solely on process. Maintain tamper-evident records of all changes to model weight systems, capturing who authorized the change, who implemented it, and what was modified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce access restrictions on model weight systems, including weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving environments, through automated mechanisms that block unauthorized change attempts and apply least privilege to write, modify, and delete operations on weights. Automatically generate audit records of enforcement actions, including denied access attempts, privilege escalations, and configuration changes to weight-related infrastructure. Protect audit records from modification by the systems or accounts they monitor, and forward them to a centralized logging environment with controls separate from the weight systems themselves. Alert on repeated or anomalous enforcement events that may indicate probing, misconfiguration, or attempted bypass.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Limit privileges to modify, deploy, or reconfigure production model weight systems, including weight repositories, serving infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and training cluster configurations, to a minimal set of explicitly authorized accounts and roles. Enforce separation between development and production weight environments such that accounts used for experimentation, fine-tuning pipelines, or testing do not carry production change privileges. Require distinct authorization paths for weight deployment, access policy changes, and backup or restore operations, so no single account or role can unilaterally complete any of these actions without additional approval. Apply technical controls that prevent production weight changes outside of controlled workflows, and restrict ad-hoc or direct modification of production weight artifacts except under documented emergency procedures with compensating oversight. Review and reevaluate production privileges at an organization-defined, risk-based frequency, and promptly reassess access when role responsibilities change, personnel actions occur, or a security incident implicates production weight systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain secure baseline configurations for all infrastructure involved in storing, training, fine-tuning, and serving model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference endpoints. Configurations should reflect the most restrictive settings consistent with operational requirements, disabling unnecessary services, enforcing encryption for weight storage and transmission, and applying hardened settings to ML framework installations and surrounding platform components. Implement the baseline configurations and use automated scanning to detect drift across the model weight environment. Identify, document, and approve deviations from baseline configurations, recording the operational justification and any compensating controls in place. Monitor configuration changes and remediate deviations according to risk priority, applying faster response to findings that directly expose model weights or the access controls protecting them.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use automated mechanisms to manage, apply, and verify configuration settings across model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference endpoints. Enforce approved security baselines through automation rather than manual configuration, and continuously verify that deployed configurations remain consistent with those baselines. Detect and alert on configuration drift, unauthorized manual changes that bypass automation, and deviations in settings governing encryption, access controls, and network exposure of weight storage and serving systems. Maintain version-controlled configuration definitions to support review, audit, and rollback of changes affecting model weight environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configure systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights to provide only the capabilities required for their defined function. Disable or remove services, protocols, ports, and software that are not required for model weight operations, including remote management interfaces not accessed through approved monitored pathways, file transfer or sharing protocols that expose weight storage to unauthorized networks, personal or consumer cloud storage clients, and unapproved data exfiltration vectors. Allow only approved, security-validated ML frameworks and libraries on training clusters, inference servers, checkpoint storage, and build pipeline nodes; prohibit installation of unapproved software on these systems without explicit authorization. Establish and maintain a documented baseline of permitted functionality for each model weight environment, review that baseline at an organization-defined frequency, and remove or disable components that are no longer operationally necessary. Document and record justification for each enabled service or capability that presents meaningful risk if abused.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Periodically review model weight systems, including weight repositories, training clusters, inference servers, checkpoint storage, and build pipelines, to identify and disable or remove unnecessary functions, ports, protocols, software, and services that increase attack surface. Scope reviews to cover network-exposed services, legacy or cleartext protocols, development and debugging tools present on production weight systems, and administrative interfaces not required for current operations. Maintain a documented approved software and services baseline for each class of model weight system, and investigate deviations from that baseline through normal security operations processes. Remediate identified unnecessary or insecure functionality within an organization-defined timeframe commensurate with the risk it represents.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict program execution on systems that store, process, or serve model weights to an approved set of software, enforcing execution controls through allowlisting, mandatory code signing, or equivalent mechanisms. Block execution from user-writable directories, temporary storage, and removable media. Require a documented security review before adding software to the approved execution set for weight-handling systems. Log and alert on execution prevention events, treating patterns indicative of unauthorized tooling, lateral movement, or exfiltration attempts as priority signals for investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain an explicit allowlist of software programs authorized to execute on systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference infrastructure. Enforce a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy through technical application control mechanisms, not policy alone, so that unauthorized software is blocked at execution, not merely discouraged. Include in the allowlist approved ML frameworks, weight management and versioning tools, data pipeline components, security and monitoring agents, and required system utilities. Require a documented security review and approval from organization-defined roles before adding new software to the allowlist, with justification proportionate to the sensitivity of the environment. Review and update the allowlist at an organization-defined frequency, removing software that is no longer operationally necessary, is no longer maintained, or has been superseded, and treat removal of unnecessary software as a routine hygiene obligation, not an exception process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain a documented inventory of all infrastructure components that store, process, transfer, or protect model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, weight repositories, inference servers, key management systems, and network components within model weight environments. Capture sufficient detail to support accountability and incident investigation, at minimum, component identity, location, ownership, software or firmware version, and role in the model weight lifecycle. Ensure the inventory is non-duplicative and accurately reflects the current environment, including components used for fine-tuning, build pipelines, and weight distribution. Establish a process to update the inventory when components are added, modified, or removed, and review it at an organization-defined frequency. Use automated discovery or asset management tooling where feasible to detect undocumented or shadow components that handle model weights, and reconcile discrepancies through a defined remediation process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automatically update the inventory of components in model weight environments, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, inference servers, build pipeline nodes, and network infrastructure with access to weight data, whenever components are added, modified, or removed. Capture attributes relevant to weight security for each component, such as its role in the weight lifecycle, its access level to weight storage or serving infrastructure, and its last security assessment. Alert on components discovered in weight-adjacent network segments that are not present in the inventory, and reconcile inventory records against network discovery on an organization-defined periodic basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Continuously monitor systems that store, train, or serve model weights for unauthorized components, including software packages, firmware, hardware peripherals, and services not present in the approved baseline inventory. Use automated mechanisms to detect deviations from the authorized component baseline at an organization-defined frequency appropriate to the risk profile of each environment. When unauthorized components are detected, automatically restrict or disable their network access or isolate the affected system, and generate alerts to authorized personnel for investigation. Require documented review and explicit authorization before any previously unauthorized component is permitted to access model weight infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce software usage restrictions on systems that store, process, or serve model weights by permitting only approved, security-validated software through application allowlisting or equivalent controls. Prohibit unauthorized ML frameworks, unapproved remote access tools, personal cloud storage clients, and peer-to-peer file sharing software on weight storage, training, and inference infrastructure. Track license compliance for software used in model weight pipelines, including training frameworks, optimization libraries, and serving stacks, to prevent use of unlicensed or improperly licensed components that may introduce legal or supply chain risk. Monitor for unauthorized software installation and alert or remediate detected violations through normal security operations processes. Conduct software inventory reviews at an organization-defined frequency to verify that weight environment software remains within approved baselines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Govern software installation on systems that store, process, or serve model weights by defining permitted and prohibited software categories, establishing an approval process for new tools, and enforcing restrictions through technical controls appropriate to the environment. On production weight storage, training clusters, and inference servers, prohibit user-initiated software installation and enforce that restriction through application controls, immutable base images, or equivalent mechanisms. For development and fine-tuning environments where users require ML tooling, require that dependencies be declared in version-controlled configuration files with cryptographic hash verification, and that new tools or frameworks receive an organization-defined level of security review before use. Prefer container-based or similarly isolated environments where the underlying host is not modifiable by users. Monitor for unauthorized software installations across model weight environments at an organization-defined frequency and investigate or remediate deviations from approved software state.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain a current inventory of all model weight artifacts, including production weights in serving infrastructure, training checkpoints, fine-tuned variants, cached copies in inference systems, and weights in backup or archival storage, documenting for each artifact its location, version, classification, ownership, and applicable access restrictions. Identify and record the personnel and service accounts with access to each location where weights are stored or processed. Document changes to weight locations as part of standard weight lifecycle operations, including movement between environments, decommissioning, and migration. Periodically audit the inventory to verify that all weight copies reside in authorized, documented locations and that access records remain accurate, with audit frequency calibrated to the risk of unauthorized weight duplication or untracked exfiltration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy automated tooling to continuously discover and catalog model weight artifacts across training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, inference servers, build pipelines, and any other infrastructure where weights may reside or transit. Maintain an authoritative inventory that captures sufficient metadata, such as weight format, origin, classification, and storage location, to verify that appropriate controls are in place for each identified instance. Alert on weights discovered outside designated secure storage locations and generate periodic reports enabling authorized personnel to identify and remediate unauthorized or uncontrolled weight instances.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate contingency planning policy and procedures for systems that store, process, or transfer model weights. Policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant environments including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure. Procedures must be sufficient to support recovery of model weight environments following incidents, including restoration of training capability and resumption of inference serving. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for managing the development, maintenance, and dissemination of contingency planning policy and procedures. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as security incidents, major changes to weight storage or serving infrastructure, or exercise findings that reveal material gaps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop and maintain a contingency plan for systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. The plan must identify essential model weight operations, including active training runs, checkpoint storage, and inference serving, and define recovery objectives and restoration priorities appropriate to the criticality of each. Address procedures for maintaining inference availability during disruptions, recovering model weight repositories from backup, resuming or reconstructing interrupted training runs, and restoring serving infrastructure without degrading the integrity or authenticity of deployed weights. Specify responsibilities and contact information for organization-defined roles involved in contingency response. Include procedures for full restoration of model weight systems without weakening the access controls, integrity verification mechanisms, or audit capabilities that were in place before the disruption. Distribute the plan to organization-defined personnel and elements with a need to execute or support it, and protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure given that it may reveal architectural details useful to adversaries. Coordinate contingency planning with incident response processes, particularly for scenarios involving suspected weight compromise, unauthorized exfiltration, or supply chain disruption. Review and update the plan at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to model weight infrastructure, storage architecture, or operational environment. Incorporate lessons from testing, exercises, and actual contingency events into subsequent plan revisions, and communicate material changes to all plan holders.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct encrypted backups of model weights, training checkpoints, fine-tuned derivatives, and associated configuration data at an organization-defined frequency consistent with recovery objectives. Back up system-level information supporting weight infrastructure, including training cluster configurations, access control settings, pipeline definitions, and key management metadata, at an organization-defined frequency. Store backups in geographically or logically separate locations with access controls equivalent to those protecting the primary weight storage environment. Protect backup confidentiality using strong encryption, integrity using cryptographic verification, and availability through redundant storage. Implement immutable or write-protected backup storage to prevent ransomware or insider modification of archived model weights. Periodically test restoration procedures to verify that weights and associated configurations can be recovered within defined recovery objectives, and document test results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypt all model weight backups using organization-approved cryptographic mechanisms that protect against unauthorized disclosure and modification, both at rest and in transit. Store encryption keys in a key management system or hardware-backed key store that is physically or logically separated from the backup storage itself, and maintain distinct keys for production weight storage and backup copies so that a single key compromise does not expose both. Require multi-party or multi-factor authorization for accessing backup encryption keys. Periodically test backup decryption to verify that cryptographic protection remains intact and that encrypted backups can be successfully restored. Store backup media or data in physically secure, geographically separated locations or distributed storage regions appropriate to the organization's recovery and threat posture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain recovery procedures for model weight systems that restore infrastructure, checkpoints, and serving environments to a verified secure state following disruption, compromise, or failure. Recovery must target organization-defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, with tighter thresholds for production serving infrastructure and relaxed thresholds for research or archival weight storage where appropriate. Before reconnecting recovered systems to weight repositories or training and serving infrastructure, verify the integrity of restored model weights and configuration using cryptographic signatures or checksums, confirm that encryption protections are active and correctly keyed, and validate that access controls and audit logging are operational. For recoveries following a confirmed or suspected security incident, require documented authorization from organization-defined security personnel before restoring weight access, and conduct a post-recovery review to determine whether the root cause has been addressed. Test recovery procedures at an organization-defined frequency, including at least one end-to-end exercise covering weight restoration, integrity verification, and access validation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and periodically update identification and authentication policy and procedures covering all personnel and services that access systems storing, training on, fine-tuning, or serving model weights. Policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, and coordination across relevant environments including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference infrastructure. Procedures must address identity verification, authenticator issuance, credential lifecycle management, and authentication requirements for both human users and automated services such as training jobs, pipeline agents, and inference endpoints. Designate an organization-defined official responsible for managing the development, maintenance, and dissemination of these policies and procedures. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as credential compromise, changes to weight-handling infrastructure, or material shifts in how weights are accessed or distributed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Uniquely identify all users accessing model weight systems and authenticate them before granting access to any weight repository, training cluster, checkpoint storage, or inference serving infrastructure. Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for all privileged access and for any access to production model weights. Apply strong authentication to standard access as well, using phishing-resistant methods where operationally feasible and at minimum using MFA. Prohibit shared credentials, hardcoded credentials in code or configuration files, and long-lived static secrets for programmatic weight access. Require programmatic access to model weights, such as from training pipelines, build systems, or serving infrastructure, to use unique, short-lived credentials scoped to the minimum necessary operations, rotated automatically. Associate all authentication events with a unique identity so that actions affecting model weights can be attributed to a specific user, service, or automated process. Federate authentication to a centralized identity provider where the environment supports it to enable consistent policy enforcement across weight repositories, training systems, and serving infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for all privileged access to model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Use cryptographic authenticators that are resistant to phishing, credential replay, and MFA fatigue attacks, such as hardware security keys or platform authenticators bound to the device, and prohibit authenticator types vulnerable to interception or social engineering, including SMS one-time codes, push notifications, and time-based software tokens. Enforce reauthentication after organization-defined periods of inactivity or elapsed session time, and when privileged access context changes materially, such as moving from a development environment to production weight storage. Monitor MFA events centrally for indicators of bypass attempts, anomalous authentication patterns, or authenticator misuse, and alert through normal security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require multi-factor authentication for all non-privileged accounts that can access model weights, weight repositories, training checkpoints, inference endpoints, or the pipelines and build systems that process weights. Apply risk-based step-up authentication that increases authentication assurance for elevated-risk contexts such as access from unrecognized devices, unusual locations, or high-volume weight retrieval, using authentication methods appropriate to the risk. Enforce lockout or progressive delay after repeated MFA failures within an organization-defined window, without prescribing fixed thresholds that may not fit operational patterns.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require multi-factor authentication for access to model weight systems such that at least one authentication factor is provided by a physical device separate from the workstation or endpoint initiating the access. Apply this requirement to both privileged and non-privileged accounts accessing weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Require that authenticator devices meet organization-defined cryptographic strength requirements appropriate to the sensitivity of model weight environments. Prohibit sole reliance on software-based authenticators running on the same device used to access model weights. Manage backup authenticators under organization-defined custody controls, limiting the number registered per user to what operational continuity requires, and review registered authenticators periodically to remove those no longer in use or authorized.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce replay-resistant authentication for all access to model weight systems, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure.
