Apply replay resistance to privileged accounts at minimum, and extend it to non-privileged accounts where access grants meaningful capability over model weights or the systems that protect them. Use authentication mechanisms whose design prevents credential reuse, such as challenge-response protocols, cryptographically bound assertions, or hardware-backed authenticators, without mandating a specific implementation. For service accounts and automated pipelines accessing weights programmatically, use certificate-based or equivalent credential mechanisms that resist replay and enforce short credential lifetimes appropriate to operational risk. Monitor authentication logs for patterns consistent with replay or credential interception attacks, and generate alerts through normal security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Provide single sign-on capability for organization-defined model weight system accounts and services, integrating weight repositories, training infrastructure, build pipelines, and inference serving systems with a centralized identity provider. Configure SSO so that disabling an account or session at the identity provider immediately revokes access across all integrated model weight systems, eliminating residual access that could persist in siloed credential stores. Enforce MFA at the identity provider before issuing authentication assertions for model weight systems. Apply organization-defined session duration limits calibrated to role sensitivity, with shorter limits for privileged or production weight access. Log SSO authentication events for model weight systems with sufficient context to support anomaly detection and investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require unique identification and authentication of devices before permitting connections to systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Use certificate-based mutual TLS, hardware-backed device identity attestation, or equivalent mechanisms that bind identity to the device rather than relying solely on user credentials. Maintain an authoritative registry of devices authorized to access model weight environments, capturing enough information to support access decisions and incident investigation. Prohibit model weight access from unmanaged or unregistered devices. Revoke device credentials and registry authorization promptly when devices are decommissioned, reported lost or stolen, or otherwise determined to no longer meet organizational access requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require cryptographic bidirectional authentication before any device establishes a connection to model weight repositories, training clusters, inference servers, or checkpoint storage. Both the device and the weight system must mutually authenticate using certificate-based identity, ensuring neither side can be impersonated. Issue device certificates from an organization-controlled PKI, and where available, bind private keys to hardware security modules or equivalent tamper-resistant storage; where hardware key protection is unavailable, enforce equivalent controls through restricted key storage, filesystem-level access controls, and key access logging. Define and enforce organization-defined certificate validity periods appropriate to the threat environment. Automatically revoke certificates for devices that are lost, decommissioned, or otherwise untrusted, and deny weight system access to any device that cannot present a valid, current certificate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require device attestation as a condition of access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, and inference serving systems. Use platform-supported attestation mechanisms, such as hardware-rooted measured boot, cloud platform attestation services, or endpoint compliance verification, to confirm that accessing devices are in a known-good, policy-compliant state before granting weight access. Verification must confirm boot integrity and the operational status of required security controls on the device. Block access from devices that fail attestation or fall outside compliance policy, and require periodic re-verification for active sessions at an organization-defined interval commensurate with the sensitivity of the weights being accessed. Monitor for attestation anomalies or patterns suggesting device compromise, and route alerts through established security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Manage identifiers for individuals, service accounts, automated pipelines, and devices that access model weight systems through an authoritative identity registry. Require documented authorization before assigning identifiers to any principal that will access weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, or inference infrastructure. Assign identifiers that distinguish between human users, service accounts, and automation, including pipeline runners, serving processes, and orchestration agents, so that audit logs can attribute access to a specific principal and purpose. Prohibit shared or generic identifiers for weight access; each service or automated process accessing weights must have a unique identifier scoped to its function. Prevent reuse of retired identifiers for an organization-defined period sufficient to ensure historical audit records remain unambiguous and that access patterns cannot be obscured by recycling old identities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Assign and maintain status attributes on all accounts with access to model weight systems, repositories, training infrastructure, and inference serving environments. Status attributes must distinguish characteristics relevant to access decisions, such as employment standing, active authorization status, and current role alignment with weight access scope. Use these attributes to drive automated access decisions, restricting or suspending access when status changes indicate that authorization is no longer valid or that risk has materially increased. Ensure that status information is visible to authorized personnel conducting access reviews, investigating anomalous activity, or evaluating access requests for weight systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Manage authenticators for all accounts and services with access to model weights, training infrastructure, weight repositories, and inference systems. Verify the identity of individuals, services, or devices before issuing credentials, and establish authenticator requirements commensurate with the sensitivity of the access being granted. Require phishing-resistant, hardware-backed authenticators for privileged accounts and for accounts with direct access to production model weights; permit software-based MFA for lower-privilege access where risk justifies it. Change default credentials on any system component involved in weight storage, training, or serving before that component is placed into operation. Rotate credentials for service accounts and automation pipelines accessing model weights at an organization-defined frequency and upon any indication of compromise or significant configuration change. Revoke or disable credentials promptly when personnel depart, change roles, or are subject to access restrictions, and establish documented procedures for handling lost or compromised authenticators that include immediate revocation and reissuance. Protect stored authenticator material, including service account secrets, API keys, and certificates used to access weight storage or serving infrastructure, using secrets management systems or hardware security modules, with access to the credential store itself subject to privileged access controls. Change credentials for shared or role-based accounts whenever membership in that role changes, and prefer eliminating shared credentials in favor of individually attributable accounts where operationally feasible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce password-based authentication requirements for accounts with access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, build pipelines, and inference serving systems. Maintain and regularly update a list of commonly used, expected, or known-compromised passwords, and verify that newly created or updated passwords are not found on that list. Transmit passwords only over cryptographically protected channels. Store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function. Require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery, and prompt or require password replacement when credentials are suspected to be compromised. Allow selection of long passwords and passphrases, permitting spaces and all printable characters, and provide tooling to assist users in selecting strong authenticators. Enforce organization-defined composition and complexity rules calibrated to the sensitivity of model weight access. Complement password authentication with phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for all accounts with direct access to model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit embedding unencrypted static authenticators, including passwords, API keys, tokens, and certificates, in source code, configuration files, container images, training scripts, pipeline definitions, checkpoint metadata, or any other artifact used to access model weight storage, training infrastructure, or serving systems. Store all such credentials in a dedicated secrets management system, inject them at runtime through secure mechanisms, and ensure they are never written to logs, weight metadata, or model artifacts. Apply automated scanning to code repositories and build pipelines that handle weight access to detect and block embedded credentials before they reach production. Use short-lived, dynamically generated credentials for service accounts and automated pipelines that access model weights, and enforce timely rotation of any static credentials that remain in use. When an embedded or exposed credential is discovered, revoke and rotate it promptly and investigate the scope of any potential exposure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Obscure authentication feedback for all systems used to access, store, process, or serve model weights. Mask or suppress display of passwords, tokens, and API keys during entry, and ensure that authentication failure messages do not reveal whether a credential, identity, or access path was valid. Apply these requirements consistently across interactive consoles, web interfaces, remote sessions, and programmatic access flows used in model weight environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure that authentication to systems storing, processing, or serving model weights relies on cryptographic modules that meet applicable regulatory and organizational validation requirements. Apply validated cryptographic authentication consistently across model weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Maintain an inventory of cryptographic modules used in weight-related environments, tracking validation status and lifecycle. Monitor for module failures, tampering indicators, or published vulnerabilities, and replace or remediate modules that fall out of compliance or reach end-of-life. Prohibit the use of unvalidated or deprecated cryptographic implementations for authenticating access to model weight systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Uniquely identify and authenticate all non-organizational users and automated processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users before granting access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, or inference serving systems. Require federated authentication through organizational or trusted identity providers where available, or issue individual time-limited credentials with multi-factor authentication for external collaborators, contractors, auditors, and managed service providers. Prohibit shared, guest, or anonymous access to any system storing or processing model weights. Apply stricter access scoping to non-organizational users than to internal personnel by default, limiting access to the minimum weight artifacts and system functions required for the defined engagement. Apply additional monitoring to non-organizational sessions, including logging of access patterns, data transfers, and privilege use. Revoke credentials and access promptly upon contract completion, role change, or any indication of misuse.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require re-authentication within active sessions before users or automated processes perform sensitive operations on model weight infrastructure, including exporting weights to external systems, modifying access control policies for weight repositories, accessing weight encryption keys, deleting or overwriting checkpoints, and altering security configurations for training or serving systems. Implement step-up authentication, requiring an additional factor, explicit approval, or both, that gates these operations independently of how recently the session was established. Use time-bound re-authentication windows scoped to the operation or an organization-defined short duration, after which re-authentication must be repeated. Log all re-authentication events and denied attempts, including the identity, operation requested, outcome, and relevant session context, and route those logs to centralized monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require identity proofing for all personnel before granting accounts that access model weight systems, resolving each identity to a unique individual before provisioning access. Validate and verify identity evidence through in-person or supervised remote processes appropriate to the sensitivity of the access being granted, with stronger verification required for privileged access to production weights, training infrastructure, or weight repositories. Maintain records of identity proofing outcomes sufficient to support audit and accountability. Reverify identity following credible indicators of credential compromise or when access is reinstated after an organization-defined period of inactivity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require verified identity evidence from individuals before granting access to model weight systems, with stronger evidence requirements for privileged or production weight access than for standard access. Accept government-issued photo identification or equivalent authoritative documentation as the baseline for privileged access provisioning, and establish proportionate evidence requirements for lower-privilege weight access roles. Maintain records linking verified identity to provisioned accounts for model weight environments, and re-verify identity at an organization-defined, risk-based interval for accounts with ongoing privileged access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Validate and verify identity evidence presented during onboarding or access requests for model weight systems using methods appropriate to the access level being granted. For privileged or production weight access, require verification against authoritative sources such as employment records or government-issued identity documents, and use automated or human-reviewed document validation capable of detecting common forgery or substitution. For remote verification, require real-time identity confirmation with liveness detection or equivalent assurance. Maintain a record of the verification method used and evidence reviewed for each access grant, sufficient to support later audit or investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require out-of-band address confirmation before activating accounts with access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, or inference serving systems. Deliver a registration code or proofing notice through a channel independent of the primary registration pathway, such as a separate email domain, verified phone number, or physical address, to confirm the user's address of record prior to granting access. Apply this requirement to privileged accounts and, at minimum, to any account with write, download, or administrative access to production model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate incident response policy and procedures covering the full lifecycle of model weight security incidents, including unauthorized access to weight repositories, weight exfiltration attempts, insider threats involving training or serving infrastructure, supply chain compromises affecting build pipelines or checkpoints, and accidental exposure of proprietary weights. Ensure the policy addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, coordination across relevant teams, and compliance obligations. Ensure procedures are actionable and specific to model weight environments, covering incident detection, classification by severity and weight sensitivity, containment, evidence preservation, escalation, notification, and post-incident review. Designate an organization-defined official responsible for maintaining and disseminating the policy and procedures. Review and update the policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant incidents, material changes to model weight infrastructure, or meaningful shifts in the threat environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Provide incident response training to personnel with roles in model weight security, scoped to their specific responsibilities. Train personnel with access to model weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, or inference infrastructure to recognize and report indicators of weight-related incidents, including unusual access patterns, unexpected weight transfers or copies, suspicious credential requests, and social engineering attempts targeting weight access. Train personnel responsible for security operations on model weight–specific incident handling, including analyzing weight access logs, identifying potential exfiltration events, preserving forensic integrity of weight repositories and audit trails, and coordinating with legal and IP stakeholders when weight theft is suspected. Update training content following model weight security incidents, significant changes to weight handling infrastructure or procedures, or at an organization-defined frequency. Deliver initial training when personnel assume a role involving model weight access or incident response responsibility, and at an organization-defined recurring interval thereafter.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain an incident handling capability covering the full lifecycle of security incidents affecting model weight environments, including preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery. Develop and maintain runbooks specific to weight-related incident scenarios, including unauthorized weight access or exfiltration, compromise of training or serving infrastructure, insider misuse of weight repositories, and supply chain tampering with model artifacts. Ensure detection capabilities are tuned to weight environment signals such as anomalous bulk downloads, unexpected weight transfers to external destinations, unusual access to checkpoint storage, or privilege escalation on training clusters. Define containment procedures that can isolate affected weight repositories, revoke or suspend access to model artifacts, and segment compromised training or serving infrastructure without unnecessarily disrupting authorized workloads. Include eradication steps appropriate to weight-specific compromise scenarios, such as credential rotation for pipeline service accounts, integrity verification of surviving weight artifacts, and removal or quarantine of tampered checkpoints. Define recovery procedures that restore weight access under verified controls and confirm integrity of weights placed back into service. Coordinate incident handling with continuity and recovery planning for training and serving infrastructure so that response actions and restoration activities remain consistent. Incorporate lessons learned from weight-related incidents and exercises into response procedures, detection logic, and preparedness activities on an ongoing basis, and ensure that response capability remains consistent and exercisable across teams and environments that handle model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Track and document security incidents affecting model weight systems, including training infrastructure, weight repositories, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving environments. Maintain a central record of incidents and candidate incidents, alerts, anomalies, and suspicious events, with sufficient detail to support investigation, escalation, and post-incident review. Capture indicators relevant to model weight compromise such as anomalous bulk access or transfer of weight files, access pattern deviations, attempts to disable protective controls, and privilege changes preceding unusual weight activity. Ensure incident records link observable events to affected systems and weight assets where determinable. Review and triage open incidents at a frequency consistent with organizational capacity and the risk profile of the environment, and escalate promptly when indicators suggest active or imminent weight exfiltration or tampering.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require personnel with access to model weight systems to report suspected security incidents, including unauthorized or anomalous weight access, potential exfiltration, credential compromise, social engineering attempts, and suspected insider activity, through documented reporting channels within an organization-defined timeframe. Maintain multiple reporting paths so that personnel can escalate without relying on a single channel that may itself be compromised. Report confirmed or credible model weight incidents to organization-defined internal authorities, legal counsel, and external parties as warranted by severity, legal obligation, or regulatory requirement. Ensure incident reports capture sufficient detail about the affected systems, weights, access patterns, and timeline to support forensic investigation and, where applicable, legal action.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop and maintain an incident response plan scoped to model weight environments that defines the organizational structure and responsibilities for responding to weight-related security incidents, describes how that capability integrates with broader organizational incident response, and identifies the categories of incidents requiring response, including unauthorized access to weight repositories, attempted or confirmed weight exfiltration, compromise of training or inference infrastructure, insider misuse of privileged weight access, and supply chain tampering with checkpoints or build pipelines. Include response playbooks or procedures for each incident category relevant to the organization's weight lifecycle, covering detection, containment, evidence preservation, recovery, and post-incident review. Define metrics for evaluating incident response effectiveness in model weight contexts, such as time to detect anomalous weight access and time to contain confirmed exfiltration. Specify the resources and management support required to sustain and mature the capability. Address information-sharing obligations and constraints, including when and how to communicate weight-related incidents to internal stakeholders, customers, or external parties. Obtain review and approval from organization-defined personnel or roles at an organization-defined frequency and whenever significant changes occur to weight infrastructure, organizational structure, or the threat environment. Distribute the plan to organization-defined incident response personnel and organizational elements. Update the plan following significant incidents, exercises, infrastructure changes, or identified gaps, and communicate changes to all relevant personnel. Protect the incident response plan itself from unauthorized access, as it contains information about defensive capabilities and response procedures that could be exploited by an adversary.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a documented response capability for unauthorized exposure or misdirection of model weights. Assign organization-defined roles with clear responsibility for leading and coordinating spillage response. When a spillage is identified, determine which specific weight artifacts are involved, including full checkpoints, fine-tuned variants, quantized derivatives, and any parameter fragments, and assess their sensitivity and lineage. Alert responsible personnel through communication channels independent of the affected systems or pipelines. Isolate affected components, which may include training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, build pipelines, inference servers, or caching layers, to contain further propagation. Eradicate unauthorized copies of model weights from affected systems using secure deletion practices appropriate to the storage medium and verified through evidence of completion. Identify secondary locations that may have received contaminated weights, including derived artifacts, cached copies, logs containing embedded parameters, or downstream services that ingested the affected weights. After containment, conduct a root-cause analysis sufficient to support corrective action and inform future preventive controls. Fulfill any applicable legal, regulatory, or contractual notification obligations as determined by organizational policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate maintenance policy and procedures for all infrastructure used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. The policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant environments including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference servers. Procedures must address approval workflows for scheduled and emergency maintenance, escort and supervision requirements for vendor or contractor personnel accessing weight-bearing systems, sanitization and verification steps before equipment is removed or repurposed, and security validation after maintenance activities that could affect weight integrity or access controls. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for maintaining and disseminating this policy. Review and update the policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant maintenance incidents, infrastructure changes, or changes in the threat environment relevant to model weight security.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain controlled maintenance procedures for infrastructure that stores, trains, or serves model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference systems. Approve and monitor all maintenance activities, whether performed on-site or remotely, before work begins, ensuring that authorized personnel or a designated oversight process sanction each activity. Require explicit approval before any storage media or compute hardware containing model weights or weight-adjacent data is removed from organizational facilities for off-site servicing or replacement. Prior to removal, apply cryptographic erase or equivalent sanitization to any media that held model weights, and verify that sanitization completed successfully. Following maintenance, repair, or replacement of any component in model weight infrastructure, verify that security controls, including encryption, access controls, audit logging, and network segmentation, remain intact and functioning as expected. Retain maintenance records containing sufficient detail to support security review and incident investigation, including the nature of the work performed, the components involved, personnel or vendors who performed or supervised the work, and confirmation of post-maintenance security verification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain an approved inventory of tools permitted for maintenance, diagnostic, and administrative use on systems that store, process, or serve model weights. Approve tools before use, applying security review focused on capabilities that introduce elevated risk in weight environments, including file transfer, bulk export, credential caching, and remote access functions. Enforce least-capability selection: where a tool's permitted function does not require file transfer or bulk data access, prohibit or disable those capabilities before use. Remove or disable maintenance tools after use on weight systems, or restrict them to dedicated maintenance accounts with limited scope. Monitor and log maintenance tool activity on weight infrastructure, and investigate usage patterns inconsistent with authorized purpose, such as unexpected data reads, connections to external endpoints, or access outside scheduled maintenance windows. Review the approved tool inventory at an organization-defined frequency to remove tools no longer needed and reassess the risk profile of retained tools.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Inspect tools and equipment used to maintain model weight infrastructure, including laptops, diagnostic hardware, and removable media, before connecting them to training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, or inference servers. Verify that maintenance tools have not been tampered with or modified in ways inconsistent with their intended purpose, including checks for malware and, where feasible, firmware integrity. Prohibit the use of personal devices for maintenance activities on model weight systems; provide organization-owned equipment for this purpose. Log all tool connections to model weight systems as part of normal maintenance session records. Inspect equipment returning from external repair or third-party custody for signs of hardware modification before returning it to service in model weight environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Inspect all media containing diagnostic tools, maintenance utilities, or test programs for malicious code before use on systems that store, process, or serve model weights. Enforce read-only media where the maintenance task permits it, and restrict writable media to explicitly authorized maintenance windows with documented justification and oversight. Apply device control policies to model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference servers, to prevent unapproved media from being mounted or executed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prevent unauthorized removal of maintenance equipment, including laptops, diagnostic tools, external drives, and portable media, from facilities or systems that store, process, or serve model weights. Before any maintenance equipment leaves a weight environment, verify that no model weight data, checkpoints, or derivative artifacts are present on the device; sanitize storage if verification cannot be confirmed. For equipment that cannot be sanitized prior to removal, retain it within the facility or destroy it in accordance with organizational media handling policy. When off-site repair or vendor return is operationally necessary and sanitization is not feasible, obtain explicit approval from organization-defined personnel, document the authorization, and apply compensating controls such as escorted transfer or chain-of-custody tracking. Maintain records of maintenance equipment that accessed weight systems, including what was brought in, what was removed, and the disposition of each item.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require all remote maintenance and diagnostic access to model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference servers, to be authorized in advance, routed through hardened bastion or jump hosts, and conducted under continuous session recording. Enforce multi-factor authentication for all remote maintenance sessions, and apply additional approval requirements before initiating remote access to production weight systems. Limit remote maintenance tool access to those explicitly authorized for use in model weight environments, and prohibit general-purpose remote access tools where dedicated, organization-approved alternatives are available. Maintain records of all remote maintenance activity, including the initiating identity, systems accessed, and actions taken, sufficient to support retrospective investigation. Terminate remote sessions and associated network connections promptly upon completion of maintenance, and verify termination automatically where feasible. Periodically review session recordings and logs from remote maintenance activity on weight-bearing systems to detect unauthorized weight access, anomalous operations, or deviations from the stated maintenance purpose.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require that nonlocal maintenance of systems that store, process, or serve model weights be performed from systems with security capabilities equivalent to or greater than the system being maintained. Where component removal is operationally feasible before nonlocal maintenance, sanitize the component of any model weight data before the session begins, inspect it for potentially malicious software after the session concludes, and restore it only after inspection passes. For maintenance sessions where component removal is not feasible, conduct sessions through an isolated administrative access path that prevents direct access to weight storage, enforce full session recording with real-time oversight by authorized personnel, and verify that no weight data was accessed or transferred beyond the scope of the maintenance activity before returning the system to production use.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a documented authorization process for personnel who perform maintenance on infrastructure that stores, processes, or serves model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference systems. Verify that unescorted maintenance personnel hold access authorizations appropriate to the systems they will work on before allowing unsupervised access. For personnel who do not hold the required authorizations, designate authorized personnel with sufficient technical competence to supervise their activities and prevent unauthorized access to model weights or the controls protecting them. Apply equivalent vetting standards to external maintenance providers as to internal personnel with comparable access. Revoke maintenance access upon completion of work and confirm that no persistent credentials, sessions, or access paths remain active. Where maintenance is performed by third-party or managed service providers, include model weight protection obligations in contractual agreements and verify compliance through periodic review.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish procedures for maintenance personnel who lack authorized access to model weight systems, including physical infrastructure such as training clusters, checkpoint storage, inference servers, and weight repositories. Require that such personnel be escorted and actively supervised by authorized personnel who hold appropriate access and are technically qualified to identify and respond to unauthorized weight access attempts during the maintenance activity. Before permitting unsupervised maintenance personnel to work on systems that store or process model weights, ensure that weights are either removed from the system, encrypted at rest with keys inaccessible to the maintenance context, or that storage media is physically disconnected and secured. Where removal or disconnection is not operationally feasible, implement compensating controls such as storage-level encryption with key quarantine, access suspension at the infrastructure level, or equivalent technical measures that prevent weight exposure during the maintenance window. Document the controls applied for each maintenance event and retain those records for accountability and audit purposes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain availability of critical spare components, replacement capacity, and vendor support agreements for infrastructure that stores, trains, or serves model weights, ensuring that hardware or service failures do not result in prolonged loss of access to weights or unrecoverable degradation of weight integrity. Identify components whose failure poses the greatest risk, including storage systems holding production or checkpoint weights, hardware security modules, and network fabric supporting training clusters, and establish supply or recovery arrangements commensurate with those risks. After maintenance or component replacement, verify that security controls protecting model weights, including encryption at rest, access enforcement, and audit logging, remain intact and correctly configured before returning systems to production use.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate media protection policy and procedures for systems and storage media that contain model weights, including training checkpoints, fine-tuned weights, and production model artifacts. Policy must address the full media lifecycle, provisioning, labeling, access control, transportation, storage, retention, and sanitization or destruction, across all environments where weights reside, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference infrastructure. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for managing and maintaining media protection policy and procedures. Review and update both policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to weight storage infrastructure, media handling practices, or the threat environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict access to physical and digital media containing model weights, including backup tapes, portable drives, offline checkpoint archives, and any removable storage used in training or serving infrastructure, to authorized personnel with a documented business need. Store weight-bearing media in physically secured locations with access limited to authorized personnel. Require explicit authorization before removing weight media from secure facilities, and apply tamper-evident measures during transport. Maintain an inventory of weight-bearing media and audit it at an organization-defined frequency to verify accountability and detect unauthorized removal or duplication.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Mark all physical and digital media containing model weights with labels that identify the sensitivity level, applicable handling restrictions, and authorized distribution boundaries. For physical media such as drives, tapes, or printed artifacts, apply durable, tamper-evident labels that remain legible throughout the media lifecycle. For digital media, embed sensitivity metadata in file system attributes, container image labels, or checkpoint manifest files so that handling requirements travel with the weights through training, storage, and serving pipelines. Exempt media from marking only when it remains within organization-defined controlled areas where access controls and physical security provide equivalent protection, and document such exemptions. Ensure personnel who handle marked media understand what each marking requires in terms of storage conditions, transfer authorization, and disposal method.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Store media containing model weights, including portable drives, backup tapes, removable storage, and decommissioned hardware from training clusters or inference servers, in physically secured locations with access control, surveillance, and intrusion detection. Restrict access to stored weight media to authorized personnel and maintain records of who accessed or handled physical media. For backup or archival media containing weights, use offsite or geographically separated storage to protect against site-level loss. Apply environmental controls appropriate to the media type to prevent degradation. Protect stored media from the point of creation or receipt until destruction or sanitization, and inspect stored weight media periodically for signs of tampering or deterioration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypt all model weight media before transport outside of controlled areas using strong encryption appropriate to the sensitivity of the weights. Apply tamper-evident packaging to physical media carrying model weights, and use tracked transport methods that provide verifiable delivery confirmation. Maintain chain of custody records for each transport event, capturing at minimum the sender, recipient, transport method, and integrity verification on receipt. Restrict transport of model weight media to authorized personnel, and prohibit transport of unencrypted weight media outside secure facilities under any circumstances. Document transport activities in a manner that supports accountability and incident investigation if media is lost, delayed, or tampered with in transit.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sanitize or destroy all media containing model weights, including training checkpoints, fine-tuned weights, and inference model files, before disposal, reuse, or release outside organizational control. Apply cryptographic erasure by destroying or revoking encryption keys for encrypted weight storage, or apply physical destruction methods such as shredding, degaussing, or incineration for unencrypted media. For cloud-hosted weight storage, use provider-provided secure deletion mechanisms and retain confirmation of deletion completion. Document each sanitization or destruction event, capturing sufficient detail to support audit and chain-of-custody verification, including media type, storage identifier, method used, date, and the authorized personnel who performed or witnessed the action. Retain destruction records for an organization-defined period. Prohibit release or disposal of weight-bearing media without verified sanitization or destruction.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict or prohibit the use of removable and portable storage media on systems that store, process, or serve model weights. Apply technical controls to enforce media restrictions on training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Where removable media use is operationally necessary, such as for air-gapped training environments or secure weight transfers, require explicit authorization, verify device ownership and registration before use, enforce encryption on the media, and scan for malicious content before and after use. Prohibit the use of any portable storage device that lacks an identifiable, registered owner. Log all authorized media use events on model weight systems and investigate anomalies or unauthorized attempts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate physical and environmental protection policy and procedures for facilities and infrastructure that store, process, or support model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference serving environments. Policy must address purpose, scope, access control requirements, environmental protection, incident response to physical breaches, and the physical security lifecycle from provisioning through decommissioning. Assign responsibility for maintaining and disseminating these policies and procedures to organization-defined personnel or roles. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant physical security incidents, infrastructure changes, or facility assessments that affect model weight environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a formal authorization process for physical access to facilities housing model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving environments. Require documented approval from organization-defined roles before granting physical access to these areas, with access scoped to the minimum areas necessary for the individual's responsibilities. Issue and manage physical access credentials through a controlled provisioning process tied to documented business need. Review the list of authorized individuals at an organization-defined, risk-based frequency, with emphasis on roles whose physical presence could enable weight exfiltration, hardware tampering, or disruption of serving infrastructure. Revoke physical access promptly when individuals change roles, leave the organization, or no longer have a justified need. Require escorts for visitors and unauthorized personnel in areas where model weights are stored or processed, and prohibit unescorted access to those areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce physical access controls at all entry and exit points to facilities housing model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, weight repositories, and inference servers. Verify individual access authorization before granting entry using electronic access control systems, physical credentials, or equivalent mechanisms. Maintain tamper-evident access logs at controlled entry and exit points, capturing sufficient identity and timing information to support investigation of unauthorized access attempts or anomalous patterns. Escort visitors in areas where model weight systems are accessible, and limit visitor activity to what is necessary for their authorized purpose. Secure physical access credentials and devices, including keys, access cards, and combination codes, using processes appropriate to the sensitivity of the areas they protect. Inventory physical access devices at an organization-defined frequency. Revoke or rekey physical access when credentials are lost or compromised, when access authorization changes, or when individuals with access are transferred or terminated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct periodic physical security checks at the perimeters of facilities and areas housing model weight storage hardware, training clusters, and inference infrastructure to detect unauthorized removal of storage media, hardware components, or devices capable of exfiltrating weights. Checks should include inspection of personnel and materials exiting sensitive areas, monitoring of physical access points for signs of tampering, and detection of unauthorized portable storage or data transfer hardware. Calibrate the frequency and method of checks to the assessed risk of physical exfiltration from each area, applying more rigorous inspection to environments where bulk weight storage or high-value checkpoints are present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain continuous (24x7) physical security staffing at facilities housing production model weight storage, training clusters, and inference infrastructure. Require at minimum two-person coverage at critical access points to prevent single-point compromise. Train physical security personnel to recognize indicators of IP theft, unauthorized data exfiltration, and tampering with weight storage systems, and ensure they are aware of the location and sensitivity of weight storage areas. Equip personnel with reliable communication links to security operations and incident response teams. Establish and document patrol and checkpoint procedures for weight storage areas, with supervisory verification at an organization-defined frequency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitor physical access to facilities that house model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, and inference servers, using surveillance cameras, access control logs, and intrusion detection appropriate to the risk of the environment. Review physical access logs at an organization-defined frequency, and conduct additional reviews upon detection of anomalous events such as off-hours access, repeated failed entry attempts, or access by individuals whose logical access has recently changed. Correlate physical access records with logical access activity to identify cases where physical presence aligns suspiciously with weight access, exfiltration events, or administrative actions. Investigate unauthorized access attempts and physical security incidents, and coordinate findings with the organization's incident response function. Ensure that physical monitoring systems, including recording and logging infrastructure, have sufficient availability controls to prevent tampering or loss of evidence during an incident.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy physical intrusion detection and surveillance coverage in areas where model weight infrastructure is housed, including storage systems, training clusters, and inference servers. Use a combination of entry-point monitoring and area coverage sufficient to detect and record unauthorized physical access attempts. Integrate alarms with an always-on security monitoring function capable of initiating a response. Retain surveillance records for an organization-defined period sufficient to support incident investigation. Monitor the surveillance and alarm systems themselves for tampering or failure, and generate alerts when detection capability is degraded or offline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and maintain an organization-wide security program plan that addresses the protection of model weights as a critical asset class across training, fine-tuning, storage, and serving environments. The plan must describe the security controls in place or planned for model weight infrastructure, including access governance, encryption, monitoring, incident response, and supply chain risk; reflect coordination across the organizational entities responsible for building, operating, and securing that infrastructure; and document management commitment and accountability for the risks associated with weight confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Assign security responsibilities to organization-defined roles and ensure the plan is approved by a senior official with authority over the risk posture of model weight systems. Review and update the plan at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to model weight infrastructure, threat environment, or organizational structure. Protect the plan itself from unauthorized disclosure and modification using access controls commensurate with its sensitivity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain an insider threat program scoped to model weight infrastructure, covering the systems and personnel involved in training, fine-tuning, storing, and serving model weights. Constitute a cross-functional team with representation from security operations, legal, HR, and the teams responsible for weight infrastructure to coordinate detection, investigation, and response. Define the scope of technical monitoring applied to weight access, including detection of anomalous access patterns, unusual bulk retrieval or exfiltration of checkpoint data, attempts to bypass access controls, and actions inconsistent with role or business need. Establish confidential reporting mechanisms through which personnel can report suspected insider activity related to model weights. Require background screening appropriate to the level of weight access granted, with periodic reassessment for personnel in high-trust roles. Develop documented procedures for insider threat incidents involving model weights, covering evidence preservation, access suspension, coordination with legal and HR, and escalation criteria. Conduct periodic training for authorized personnel and their managers on recognizing and reporting indicators of insider risk in model weight environments. Balance monitoring scope and methods against applicable legal requirements, privacy obligations, and organizational policy, and document the boundaries of that monitoring clearly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate personnel security policies and procedures covering systems and roles involved in storing, training, fine-tuning, and serving model weights. Policies must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant organizational units. Procedures must be sufficient to implement the policy in practice across model weight environments, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles to own the development, maintenance, and dissemination of these policies and procedures. Review and update policies and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following personnel security incidents or significant changes to model weight infrastructure, access patterns, or organizational structure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Screen individuals prior to granting access to model weight systems, using background checks calibrated to the risk level of the position. For roles with direct access to model weights, including weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems, conduct checks appropriate to that access level, which may include identity verification, employment history, criminal history, and education verification. For roles with privileged access to model weight environments, apply additional screening commensurate with the elevated risk those roles represent. Establish organization-defined conditions that trigger rescreening, such as a change in role, significant expansion of access scope, or other indicators of elevated risk, and conduct rescreening at a frequency appropriate to the sensitivity of ongoing access. Follow applicable legal and regulatory requirements governing employment screening in all relevant jurisdictions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Assign a risk designation to all organizational positions, calibrated to reflect the nature and level of access the role requires to model weights and related infrastructure. Positions with direct access to model weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, or inference serving systems and particularly those with privileged or administrative access to these environments should receive risk designations commensurate with the potential impact of insider misuse, negligence, or compromise. Use risk designations to inform the level of background screening required for individuals filling those positions and the scope of access authorizations appropriate to each role. Establish screening criteria appropriate to each designation level before filling positions, and review and update position risk designations at an organization-defined frequency or when the duties or access requirements of a position materially change.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require enhanced personnel screening for individuals with privileged access to model weights, training infrastructure, weight repositories, or serving systems. Screening criteria should go beyond standard employment verification to include financial background checks, criminal history review, employment and education verification, and professional reference checks, calibrated to the sensitivity of the access being granted. For roles with the broadest or most consequential access to model weights, such as those capable of bulk exfiltration, unauthorized copying, or modification of production weights, apply the most rigorous screening criteria the organization defines for this tier. Establish a periodic rescreening cadence for privileged weight access personnel, with frequency defined by the organization based on role sensitivity and risk. Suspend or restrict weight access when screening lapses, adverse information is identified, or a personnel action warrants review, pending completion of the defined screening process. Document screening requirements by access tier, maintain records of completed screening, and align rescreening triggers with personnel management and security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Upon termination of an individual's employment, disable access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, serving systems, and any associated administrative interfaces within an organization-defined time period. Revoke or rotate all authenticators, credentials, API keys, and cryptographic material including signing keys and access tokens associated with the individual, including any credentials used to access weight pipelines or automated systems operating under that individual's identity. Conduct exit interviews that include discussion of confidentiality obligations regarding model weights and proprietary training data, post-employment restrictions where applicable, and the individual's obligations to report any subsequent discovery of unauthorized weight access or exfiltration. Retrieve security-related organizational property associated with weight system access, including hardware authentication tokens, access cards, and any portable media containing weight files or related artifacts. For individuals terminated for cause or under circumstances suggesting elevated insider risk, prioritize immediate disablement of access to weight environments before or concurrent with notification where operationally feasible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When personnel are reassigned or transferred, promptly review and revoke access to model weight repositories, training infrastructure, checkpoint storage, inference serving systems, and any related cryptographic material that is no longer required by the new role. Adjust access authorizations to reflect the operational needs of the new assignment before or immediately upon the transfer taking effect, applying least-privilege principles to the incoming role. Notify organization-defined personnel responsible for weight security and access management within an organization-defined period following the formal transfer action, and document all access changes with justification. For transfers that involve a material change in model weight access, such as moving from a role with broad training cluster access to one with no such need, or gaining new access to production weight repositories, require explicit re-authorization before access is granted rather than inheriting prior access. Verify that any shared credentials, service account memberships, or signing keys associated with the prior role are rotated or reassigned as appropriate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require all personnel, contractors, and third parties to sign access agreements before being granted access to model weights, weight repositories, training infrastructure, or serving systems. Agreements must address permitted uses of model weights, prohibitions on unauthorized copying, exfiltration, or redistribution of weights, obligations to report suspected security incidents or policy violations, and consequences of non-compliance. Include confidentiality provisions appropriate to the sensitivity of the weights being accessed. Review and update agreements when access policies materially change, and require re-signing upon update or at an organization-defined frequency. Maintain signed agreements in a manner that supports audit and accountability review.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and document personnel security requirements for external personnel, including contractors, vendors, and third-party service providers, who access model weight repositories, training infrastructure, fine-tuning pipelines, or inference serving systems. Apply background screening, onboarding security requirements, and access provisioning standards equivalent to those applied to internal personnel with comparable access. Define the scope of authorized weight-related activities in contractual agreements, and require external personnel to complete relevant security training before being granted access to model weight environments. Require external providers to notify organization-defined personnel within an organization-defined timeframe when external personnel who hold credentials, system privileges, or access rights to model weight environments are transferred, reassigned, or terminated. Revoke or suspend access to model weight systems promptly upon contract end, role change, or notification of termination, and audit that revocation has occurred. Monitor provider compliance with these requirements through periodic reviews and access audits at a frequency commensurate with the sensitivity of the weights and the scope of provider access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and enforce a formal sanctions process for personnel who fail to comply with model weight security policies, including acceptable use, access controls, handling procedures, and incident reporting requirements. Apply sanctions proportionate to the nature and severity of the violation, distinguishing between inadvertent policy gaps, negligent mishandling of weights, and deliberate actions such as unauthorized exfiltration, intentional access bypass, or insider theft. Notify organization-defined personnel or roles when a formal sanctions action is initiated, identifying the individual and the basis for the action. Coordinate with legal counsel for serious violations where criminal referral, civil action, or contractual remedy may be appropriate. Communicate the existence and scope of the sanctions process to all personnel with access to model weight systems as a deterrent, and review the process periodically to confirm it remains consistent with current policy and organizational risk posture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Incorporate security and privacy responsibilities into the position descriptions of all roles with access to model weights or related infrastructure. For roles with direct access to weight repositories, training systems, checkpoint storage, or serving infrastructure, position descriptions should identify the security responsibilities associated with that access, including expectations around acceptable use, handling of weight files, participation in security monitoring and review processes, and reporting obligations for suspected incidents or policy violations. For roles with privileged or administrative access to model weight environments, position descriptions should additionally reflect the elevated accountability associated with those privileges. Ensuring that security responsibilities are explicit in position descriptions supports appropriate role-based training, clearer accountability, and informed screening and authorization decisions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate risk assessment policy and supporting procedures for systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. The policy must address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant environments including training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference servers. Procedures must be sufficient to support consistent execution of risk assessments across those environments, including assessment of threats to weight confidentiality and integrity, insider risk, and supply chain exposure. Designate an organization-defined official responsible for maintaining the policy and procedures. Review and update the policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as major infrastructure changes, weight exfiltration incidents, or material shifts in the threat environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Categorize model weights and the systems that store, process, transfer, or serve them based on the potential impact of unauthorized disclosure, modification, or loss. Account for factors specific to model weight environments, including the sensitivity of training data incorporated into weights, the capability and potential for misuse of the model, the competitive or operational value of proprietary architectures and checkpoints, and dependencies between weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, and inference infrastructure. Document the categorization decision and its supporting rationale, and ensure it is reviewed and approved by authorized decision-makers with appropriate authority. Revisit categorization when significant changes occur, such as new model capabilities, changes to training data sensitivity, expansion of serving scope, or organizational risk posture shifts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct risk assessments for systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights, covering threats relevant to model weight environments such as insider exfiltration, external compromise of weight repositories or training clusters, supply chain interference with build pipelines, and unauthorized access through serving infrastructure. Assess the likelihood and potential impact of model weight exposure, including loss of proprietary model IP, enabling of adversarial attacks, or competitive harm. Integrate findings with broader organizational risk management decisions and document results in a form appropriate to the organization. Review and update risk assessments at an organization-defined frequency and whenever significant changes occur to model weight infrastructure, hosting environments, access control architecture, or the threat landscape affecting AI model assets. Disseminate results to organization-defined personnel with responsibility for model weight security decisions, and track remediation of identified findings through existing risk management processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Assess supply chain risks for components that directly store, process, transfer, or protect model weights, including ML frameworks, training and inference hardware, weight repository services, cloud infrastructure, build pipeline tooling, and security controls applied to weight environments. Evaluate each component's exposure to tampering, unauthorized access, and integrity compromise across its acquisition, deployment, and update lifecycle. Factor in vendor security practices, dependency chains, and the potential for malicious or compromised updates to reach weight storage or serving systems. Reassess at an organization-defined frequency and whenever a significant change occurs in the supply chain, such as a vendor acquisition, a material shift in a component's provenance, a disclosed vulnerability in a weight-adjacent dependency, or a change to the organization's weight infrastructure that introduces new third-party dependencies. Maintain documented fallback options for critical weight infrastructure dependencies where substitution is feasible, and prioritize components with auditable integrity assurances for the highest-risk positions in the weight lifecycle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct vulnerability scanning across infrastructure used to store, train, serve, and transfer model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, model repositories, inference servers, and the build and orchestration pipelines that interact with them. Perform scanning at an organization-defined frequency and upon discovery of vulnerabilities with credible relevance to these environments, using authenticated scanning where technically feasible to surface configuration weaknesses and privilege escalation risks that unauthenticated scans miss. Include ML framework dependencies, container images used in training and serving workloads, and software components in the weight access path within the scope of vulnerability monitoring. Analyze scan results and prioritize remediation based on organizational risk assessment, accounting for the sensitivity of weights accessible through the affected system, exploitability, and exposure. Remediate confirmed vulnerabilities within organization-defined timeframes aligned to severity. Share relevant vulnerability findings with authorized personnel responsible for related model weight infrastructure to reduce exposure across similar environments. Maintain current vulnerability definitions and update scanning tool coverage as new vulnerability classes emerge, including those affecting ML-specific frameworks and orchestration tooling.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain current vulnerability definitions for all systems that store, train, serve, or otherwise process model weights, updating scanning configurations promptly when new vulnerabilities are identified through security advisories, vendor disclosures, or internal discovery. Subscribe to security advisories for ML frameworks and libraries used in weight storage, training, and inference pipelines, and update scanners when relevant vulnerabilities are published. Prioritize scanning coverage for vulnerability classes that pose elevated risk in model weight environments, including deserialization flaws, model checkpoint loading exploits, and remote code execution vulnerabilities in training and serving infrastructure. Trigger additional scans following significant changes to weight storage systems, training clusters, or inference infrastructure, and after relevant vulnerability disclosures that may affect those environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Define and document the breadth and depth of vulnerability scanning coverage across all systems involved in storing, training, serving, and protecting model weights. Coverage must span training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, inference servers, build and fine-tuning pipelines, and the orchestration and access control systems that govern them. Scanning must address operating systems, container images, dependencies, and ML framework components used in weight environments. Use authenticated scanning where feasible to enable deeper inspection of components that unauthenticated scans cannot reach. Ensure coverage extends across development, staging, and production weight environments, not only production. Identify and document gaps in scanning coverage, and apply compensating controls where automated scanning cannot reach.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Grant vulnerability scanning systems privileged read access to model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, inference servers, and build pipelines, sufficient to perform deep inspection of system configurations, installed packages, running processes, network connections, and weight-adjacent file systems. Restrict scanner credentials to read-only access to prevent unintended modification of weights or supporting infrastructure. Manage scanner accounts through the same provisioning and review processes used for other privileged accounts in model weight environments, including periodic access review and credential rotation at an organization-defined frequency. Log all privileged scanner activity and integrate those logs with normal security monitoring to detect scanner credential misuse or unauthorized access attempts against weight systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish a public vulnerability disclosure program covering systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. Publish a clear security contact and submission process, acknowledge received reports within an organization-defined period, and provide status updates at a cadence appropriate to the severity and complexity of the reported issue. Coordinate with reporters on disclosure timing to allow remediation before public release. Prohibit legal action against good-faith security researchers operating within the scope of the program. Review disclosed vulnerabilities not only for remediation but for systemic patterns relevant to model weight protection infrastructure, such as weaknesses in weight repositories, checkpoint pipelines, or inference serving systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Respond to security findings affecting model weights, including results from assessments, monitoring, audits, and threat intelligence, by selecting and implementing risk responses commensurate with organizational risk tolerance and the value of the affected weights. Acceptable response options include accepting residual risk with documented justification, mitigating risk through additional or strengthened controls on weight storage, training infrastructure, or serving systems, transferring risk through contractual or insurance mechanisms where appropriate, or avoiding risk by restricting or discontinuing high-risk weight operations. Prioritize responses based on assessed likelihood and impact of weight theft, exfiltration, or unauthorized modification. Document each response decision with supporting rationale, assigned accountability, and expected outcome. Reassess risk responses when threat conditions, weight value, or operational context changes materially.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Perform criticality analysis to identify and prioritize model weights and the infrastructure that stores, trains, and serves them based on factors such as competitive value, operational dependency, replication cost, and the potential impact of theft, loss, or degradation. Use criticality determinations to tier protection controls, weights representing significant competitive advantage or operational dependency receive stronger access, encryption, monitoring, and exfiltration controls than experimental or deprecated weights. Document criticality assignments, the rationale behind them, and the protection requirements they drive. Review and update criticality determinations at organization-defined intervals and whenever a model's deployment status, business value, or threat context changes materially. Use this analysis to focus security investment where risk is highest rather than applying uniform controls across all weight assets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles acquisition and development policy and procedures covering systems that store, train on, fine-tune, or serve model weights. Policy must address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across teams involved in procuring or building model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference platforms. Designate an organization-defined official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of this policy. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant events such as acquisition of new training infrastructure, adoption of new ML frameworks, or material changes to how model weights are stored or served.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify and allocate resources necessary to protect model weights across the full lifecycle of storage, training, fine-tuning, and serving. Resource planning must account for security functions specific to model weight environments, including encryption and key management infrastructure, access control systems for weight repositories and training clusters, monitoring and anomaly detection for weight access and exfiltration risk, and personnel with sufficient expertise to operate and oversee these controls. Establish a discrete, visible budget allocation for model weight security so that protection requirements are not subordinated to operational or compute priorities. Calibrate resource levels to the criticality of the weights being protected, and review allocations when security assessments, incidents, or material changes to the model weight environment reveal gaps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Integrate security into the full lifecycle of model weight systems, from initial architecture and training pipeline design through fine-tuning, deployment, and decommissioning. At each phase, apply security activities appropriate to the risks introduced: conduct threat modeling before committing to training infrastructure or weight storage architectures; enforce secure development practices in pipeline code that processes, transforms, or exports weights; perform security testing of training and serving pipelines before production use; scan dependencies and base environments for known vulnerabilities; require a documented security review before promoting weights or serving infrastructure to production; and apply secure decommissioning procedures when retiring models or checkpoints, including verified deletion or destruction of weight artifacts. Define and assign security responsibilities for model weight systems across lifecycle phases, covering both the weights themselves and the infrastructure that builds, stores, and serves them. Incorporate weight-related risks into organizational risk management processes so that decisions about training runs, model updates, and infrastructure changes reflect current threat context. Require security checkpoints at major phase transitions, particularly before moving weights from development or staging into production serving environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Include model weight security requirements explicitly in acquisition contracts, statements of work, and procurement documentation for infrastructure, services, and tooling used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. Requirements must address: functional security capabilities expected of the acquired system or component, including access control, encryption at rest and in transit, audit logging, and secure interfaces for weight access; assurance expectations such as supply chain transparency, provenance documentation, and vulnerability management practices; documentation the vendor must provide covering the security architecture of the delivered system and the environment in which it is intended to operate; protection obligations for any security documentation or weight artifacts shared with the vendor; allocation of responsibility between the organization and vendor for security controls, incident response, and supply chain risk; and acceptance criteria that include verification of security capabilities before the system or component is placed into production weight environments. Require vendors handling model weights or components of weight infrastructure to provide timely notification of security incidents, vulnerabilities, or supply chain compromises affecting delivered systems. Define acceptance testing procedures that confirm security requirements are met prior to deployment into training, checkpoint storage, or inference environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require vendors supplying infrastructure used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights to provide functional descriptions of the security controls embedded in their products or services. Documentation must cover how those controls operate, not merely assert that they exist, including access enforcement mechanisms, encryption at rest and in transit for weight data, audit logging capabilities relevant to weight access and transfer, and how vulnerabilities in the product are identified and addressed.
