Where the product plays a direct role in protecting weight confidentiality or integrity, require vendors to provide architectural documentation sufficient to assess whether the control behavior aligns with organizational requirements before acquisition. Incorporate weight confidentiality and integrity requirements into procurement specifications so that vendor security claims can be evaluated against documented organizational needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require vendors and developers supplying components used to store, process, train, or serve model weights to provide sufficient design and implementation information to evaluate the security of those components. At minimum, require architecture documentation showing data flows, trust boundaries, and interfaces relevant to weight access and protection. For components with privileged access to weights, such as training orchestration software, checkpoint storage systems, or inference serving infrastructure, require detailed design documentation, security-relevant interface specifications, or independent security assessment reports sufficient to support the organization's own risk evaluation. For closed-source components, require evidence of third-party security assessment in lieu of source-level documentation where source access is not obtainable. Include contractual provisions ensuring continued access to documentation or audit rights if vendor support is discontinued for components critical to weight infrastructure integrity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require that external vendors, cloud providers, and system integrators delivering infrastructure used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights provide components with secure configurations enabled by default, including encryption at rest and in transit, disabled unnecessary services and network interfaces, authenticated access required from first use, and audit logging active on delivery. Ensure that these secure defaults persist across reinstallation, upgrade, and redeployment cycles, so that reconfiguring a weight repository, training cluster, inference server, or checkpoint storage system does not silently revert to an insecure state. Obtain or produce hardening guidance specific to AI workload environments from vendors where it exists, and validate delivered configurations against organizational security baselines in a staging or pre-production environment before connecting systems to production weight storage or serving infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require vendors and developers supplying software, hardware, or services used in model weight storage, training, fine-tuning, or serving infrastructure to document all network functions, ports, protocols, and services their components use or require during operation. Use this documentation to inform network segmentation decisions, firewall configuration, and attack surface reduction for weight-handling environments. Identify and disable or block any vendor-documented functions or services not required for weight operations, and treat undocumented network behavior as a risk requiring resolution before deployment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Procure hardware authenticators and identity verification products for model weight infrastructure access from an organization-maintained approved list that establishes minimum assurance requirements for phishing-resistant authentication. Verify that authenticators used to access weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems meet those assurance requirements before deployment, and remove or replace authenticators that fall out of compliance with current organizational standards.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain current documentation for systems and components that store, train, serve, or otherwise handle model weights, covering secure configuration and operation of training clusters, checkpoint storage, inference serving infrastructure, and build pipelines; effective use and maintenance of security functions such as access controls, encryption, and audit mechanisms; and known vulnerabilities or misconfigurations relevant to privileged or administrative functions in those environments. Maintain user-facing documentation describing how authorized personnel interact securely with model weight repositories and serving systems, including their responsibilities for protecting weights during access, transfer, and deployment. Where documentation for a third-party component, such as a framework, orchestration platform, or storage backend, is unavailable or insufficient to assess its security posture, record that gap and take organization-defined compensating or risk-acceptance actions. Distribute documentation to organization-defined personnel or roles based on their function, and protect documentation from unauthorized access, as it may reveal exploitable details about weight storage architecture or security controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Apply security engineering principles throughout the design, development, implementation, and modification of systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights. Ground architectural decisions in defense in depth, ensuring that no single control failure exposes weights to unauthorized access or exfiltration. Enforce least privilege and separation of duties across weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure, so that no individual or service has unilateral control over both weight access and the controls that govern it. Design systems to fail secure, defaulting to weight access denial when authentication, authorization, or integrity verification cannot be completed successfully. Ensure complete mediation by routing all weight access requests through enforced policy checks rather than relying on perimeter controls alone. Document the security principles applied to each major architectural component and the rationale for key design decisions. Review the architecture at an organization-defined frequency and after significant changes to weight infrastructure, threat environment, or adversary capability, adjusting controls where gaps or weakened assumptions are identified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish requirements for any external service provider, including cloud training platforms, managed inference services, weight hosting providers, and third-party build or fine-tuning infrastructure, that stores, processes, transmits, or otherwise handles model weights. Define and document the security controls expected of each provider, the organization's oversight responsibilities, and the roles authorized to engage or manage external services on behalf of the organization. Require providers to support encryption of model weights at rest using customer-managed keys, to notify the organization promptly of security incidents affecting weight-related systems, and to permit or supply sufficient logging and audit evidence to support the organization's monitoring obligations. Assess provider security posture before onboarding and at organization-defined intervals thereafter, with more frequent review for providers handling production or high-value weights. Establish contractual obligations that enforce these requirements and specify consequences for non-compliance, including rights to audit, suspend access, or terminate service. Monitor provider access and actions affecting model weights through log collection and alerting integrated with normal security operations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct a documented risk assessment before acquiring or outsourcing any external service that will store, process, transmit, or otherwise have access to model weights or the infrastructure that protects them. The assessment must address the vendor's security practices relevant to model weight handling, data sovereignty and jurisdictional constraints, insider threat controls, incident response and breach notification capabilities, and the scope of access granted. Require explicit organizational approval from organization-defined roles before onboarding any such external service, and document the risk acceptance decision including any residual risks and compensating controls. Revisit the assessment when the vendor's role, access scope, or threat landscape materially changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require external service providers supporting model weight infrastructure, including cloud training platforms, checkpoint storage services, inference hosting providers, and managed MLOps tooling, to formally document all functions, network ports, protocols, APIs, and data flows required to deliver their services. Use that documentation to validate network segmentation design, enforce allowlist-based connectivity controls, and identify any provider access paths that could reach, copy, or exfiltrate model weights. Prohibit undocumented connectivity between provider systems and weight storage or serving infrastructure, and review provider-documented access requirements at an organization-defined frequency or when provider configurations materially change.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict the storage, processing, and serving of model weights to organization-defined locations, including approved geographic regions, cloud provider environments, and physical facilities, based on documented risk, legal, and operational requirements. Ensure that external services handling model weights, including cloud training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference infrastructure, are contractually bound to maintain weights within approved locations and prohibited from transferring or replicating weights outside those boundaries without explicit authorization. Implement technical controls that enforce location restrictions at the infrastructure level, such as region-locked storage configurations and network-enforced egress boundaries, rather than relying solely on contractual commitments. Periodically verify provider compliance with location requirements through audits, provider attestations, or equivalent assurance mechanisms commensurate with the sensitivity of the weights involved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce configuration management practices across the full lifecycle of model weight development and deployment, covering training code, model architectures, weight checkpoints, fine-tuning pipelines, inference configurations, and supporting infrastructure. Maintain version-controlled repositories for all configuration items associated with model weight systems, with access controls, audit logging, and approval workflows governing changes to production or release-candidate artifacts. Implement only organization-approved changes to weight repositories, training cluster configurations, serving infrastructure, and associated security controls, and document the security and privacy impact of each approved change before it is applied. Establish baseline configurations for inference systems and weight storage environments, track deviations from those baselines, and remediate unauthorized or undocumented changes through a defined review process. Track security flaws identified in model weight pipelines, training infrastructure, and serving systems, manage flaw resolution through the same configuration management process, and report findings to organization-defined personnel responsible for weight security. Integrate configuration integrity checks into build and deployment pipelines so that unsigned, unreviewed, or out-of-policy artifacts cannot be promoted to production weight storage or serving environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require that security testing and evaluation be performed at each post-design stage of the development lifecycle for systems that store, train, serve, or otherwise process model weights. Testing must cover components specific to model weight environments, including weight repositories, training pipelines, checkpoint storage, inference serving infrastructure, and APIs that expose or transfer weights. Testing activities must include, at minimum, integration testing of access controls and encryption applied to weight storage and transmission, and security-focused evaluation of build pipelines and serving systems where unauthorized access or exfiltration of weights is a plausible risk. Produce evidence of completed testing activities and their outcomes. Establish a flaw remediation process that tracks identified security deficiencies to resolution and prioritizes flaws that could expose model weights to unauthorized access, exfiltration, or tampering. Correct identified flaws before production deployment where feasible, or document and accept residual risk through an authorized exception process where not. Apply the same testing requirements to third-party components integrated into model weight pipelines, including container images, custom ML frameworks, and inference runtimes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require static code analysis as part of the build pipeline for custom software that accesses, transfers, manages, or protects model weights, including weight serving code, training orchestration, checkpoint management, and access control logic. Configure analysis to detect vulnerability classes relevant to model weight access paths, such as injection flaws, insecure deserialization, authentication bypasses, and improper privilege handling. Integrate analysis into CI/CD pipelines so that findings above an organization-defined severity threshold block promotion to production environments. Document analysis results and ensure developers address identified findings before weight-handling code reaches production systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require that threat modeling and vulnerability analysis be performed for systems and components involved in model weight development, training, storage, transfer, and serving. Threat modeling must account for the confidentiality and integrity risks specific to model weights, including unauthorized access to weight repositories, exfiltration through training or inference infrastructure, insider theft via privileged access paths, and supply chain compromise through build pipelines or third-party components. Analysis must examine trust boundaries between components, such as those between training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and serving systems, and identify attack vectors that could enable weight theft, tampering, or unauthorized replication. Conduct analysis at a level of rigor appropriate to the sensitivity of the weights and the complexity of the environment, and produce documented evidence of findings, including identified threats, assessed risk levels, and planned or implemented mitigations. Update threat models when weight system architecture changes materially, such as when new serving paths, storage backends, or pipeline integrations are introduced. Integrate threat modeling outputs into design reviews for weight infrastructure changes so that findings inform access control, network segmentation, and build pipeline decisions before deployment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a documented development process for model weight pipelines, training infrastructure, and serving systems that explicitly addresses security requirements, identifies approved tools and configurations, and governs how changes to the process or tooling are managed and reviewed. Require that toolchains used in weight handling code, including training scripts, checkpoint management utilities, and inference serving components, are tracked, version-pinned, and sourced from controlled, integrity-verified repositories. Enforce code review requirements for changes that affect weight access controls, serialization and deserialization logic, and pipeline components that move or transform weights between environments. Implement integrity verification such as signing or hashing for artifacts produced by the development pipeline before they are used in training, fine-tuning, or production serving. Maintain audit records of changes to tooling configurations and development process controls sufficient to detect unauthorized modifications. Review the development process, tooling, and configurations at an organization-defined frequency and following significant incidents or changes to model weight infrastructure to verify they continue to meet current security requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct criticality analysis for components involved in storing, training, fine-tuning, and serving model weights to identify which components, if compromised or degraded, would directly enable weight theft, unauthorized exfiltration, or integrity loss. Perform this analysis at organization-defined decision points in the development lifecycle, including at minimum before initial deployment and when significant changes are made to weight storage, access control, or serving infrastructure. Apply proportionally greater development rigor, security testing, and code review to components assessed as high-criticality, such as those governing access enforcement, weight encryption, audit pipelines, and checkpoint integrity verification. Use the criticality analysis to drive prioritization of security activities rather than to satisfy a documentation requirement, and revisit assessments when the threat environment or system architecture changes materially.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require that systems storing, training, or serving model weights expose only the interfaces, APIs, and network services necessary for their defined operational function. Explicitly justify and document each external interface on weight-handling infrastructure, and remove or disable development tools, debug endpoints, and administrative interfaces that are not required in production. During design reviews for new or modified weight-handling systems, conduct an attack surface analysis that identifies interfaces providing access to weights, enumerates trust boundaries, and drives a reduction of unnecessary exposure before deployment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain a current inventory of system components used in model weight infrastructure, including operating systems, ML frameworks, container base images, accelerator firmware, and storage systems, and identify components that have reached end of support or will do so within an organization-defined planning horizon. Replace unsupported components in weight storage, training, and serving environments before support expires where operationally feasible. Where immediate replacement is not feasible, isolate unsupported components from broader network access, apply compensating controls such as enhanced monitoring and restricted access, document the residual risk, and maintain an active remediation plan. Prioritize replacement in production weight environments over development or experimental infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and disseminate policy and procedures governing the protection of systems and communications that store, process, transmit, or serve model weights. Policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across model weight environments including training clusters, weight repositories, build and fine-tuning pipelines, inference serving infrastructure, and checkpoint storage. Procedures must support consistent implementation of controls across those environments. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for managing, reviewing, and updating this policy and associated procedures. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to model weight infrastructure, threat landscape, or operational practices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Separate model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference servers, from general-purpose user environments and business application systems. Do not host production model weights on systems that also serve corporate applications, developer workstations, or shared services. Provide dedicated administrative interfaces for weight infrastructure that are distinct from general enterprise IT management planes. Apply network segmentation to isolate weight storage and serving environments from corporate networks, restricting lateral access paths that could allow a compromised general-purpose system to reach weight assets. Document the separation architecture and enforce it through change management processes so that new deployments, integrations, or infrastructure changes do not inadvertently collapse boundaries between weight environments and lower-trust systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prevent unauthorized transfer of model weight data through shared system resources by enforcing isolation boundaries at the memory, storage, and compute layers. Clear or sanitize memory regions used to load, process, or cache model weights before releasing those regions to other processes or tenants. Assign model weight storage to dedicated volumes or filesystems logically or physically separated from general-purpose data. In multi-tenant training or inference environments, enforce strong isolation between tenants using container, VM, or hardware-level boundaries that prevent cross-tenant access to weight data, activations, or intermediate checkpoints. For frontier or high-sensitivity models, prefer dedicated infrastructure over shared compute where operationally feasible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protect model weight storage, training, and serving infrastructure against denial-of-service conditions that could disrupt weight access, checkpoint writes, or inference availability. Apply resource quotas and rate limits to API endpoints and interfaces used to retrieve, upload, or serve model weights, preventing any single user, service, or process from monopolizing compute, storage, or network resources. Deploy load balancing and capacity management controls for weight-serving infrastructure to sustain availability under legitimate traffic spikes without degrading access for authorized workloads. For internet-facing weight-serving endpoints, implement network-level protections against volumetric attacks appropriate to the exposure and criticality of the service. Monitor training clusters and weight repositories for resource exhaustion conditions, including storage saturation, memory pressure, and network congestion, and alert when thresholds indicate degradation or potential abuse. Maintain documented response procedures for denial-of-service conditions affecting critical weight infrastructure, including escalation paths and fallback options for time-sensitive training or serving operations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce network segmentation that isolates model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference serving systems, from corporate networks and general-purpose environments. Implement deny-by-default boundary controls at all interfaces connecting weight infrastructure to other network zones, permitting only explicitly authorized traffic flows. Deploy managed interfaces with authentication and authorization enforcement for any external or cross-zone access to model weights, including API-layer controls for inference endpoints that handle weight-serving traffic. Restrict outbound connections from training and storage systems to the minimum required for legitimate operations, limiting pathways that could be used for bulk weight exfiltration. Isolate weight repositories and checkpoint storage in dedicated network security zones with access controls enforced at the boundary, not solely at the application layer. Monitor boundary traffic on interfaces to and from weight infrastructure for anomalies, including unusual transfer volumes, unexpected destinations, or access patterns inconsistent with normal training, fine-tuning, or serving workflows. Require remote access to weight infrastructure to traverse authenticated, encrypted, and logged access paths subject to the same boundary controls as internal access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Limit external network connections to infrastructure that stores, trains, or serves model weights to the minimum number required for legitimate operational needs. Route external access to weight storage, training clusters, checkpoint repositories, and inference serving infrastructure through organization-defined centralized gateway points with traffic inspection and logging. Prohibit direct internet connectivity for systems that store or transfer model weights at rest or in transit. Document and periodically review each authorized external connection, removing any that are no longer operationally justified. Deploy network controls that enforce these boundaries and alert on unauthorized or anomalous external connection attempts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Implement managed interfaces for all external network connections to model weight infrastructure, including connections to cloud providers, training clusters, weight repositories, inference endpoints, and build pipelines. Define explicit traffic flow policies for each managed interface that permit only authorized protocols, services, and destinations, and deny all other traffic by default. Protect the confidentiality and integrity of model weight data in transit across external connections using organization-managed encryption, ensuring that encryption keys are not exposed to external service providers without explicit authorization. Document each exception to an established traffic flow policy with a stated operational justification, responsible owner, and defined expiration; review exceptions at an organization-defined frequency and remove any that are no longer supported by a current business or operational need. Prevent unauthorized exchange of control plane traffic between model weight infrastructure and external networks, and filter such traffic at managed interface boundaries. Monitor external interfaces for traffic patterns indicative of unauthorized weight exfiltration, such as anomalous outbound data volumes, connections to unexpected destinations, or use of protocols inconsistent with defined policies, and generate alerts through established security operations processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce default-deny network policies at all boundaries protecting model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Permit only explicitly authorized traffic flows, and require documented business justification for each allowed connection covering the source, destination, protocol, and operational need. Apply deny-by-default rules at managed interfaces such as firewalls, security groups, and network access controls governing weight storage and training environments. Treat any new connection request to weight infrastructure as denied until reviewed and approved by organization-defined personnel responsible for network security. Periodically review allow-listed rules and remove those that no longer correspond to active, justified operational needs. Block protocols and services at weight network boundaries that serve no authorized function in model training, storage, or serving workflows.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prohibit split tunneling for remote connections to model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems. Enforce full-tunnel routing for all sessions that access model weights, ensuring traffic is subject to organizational monitoring and filtering controls rather than bypassing them via local internet breakout. Where split tunneling is operationally necessary for non-weight traffic, implement policy-based routing that enforces full-tunnel routing for weight-related destinations regardless of the general tunnel configuration, and verify enforcement through technical controls rather than relying solely on client configuration. Detect and alert on split tunnel configurations or bypass attempts affecting model weight access paths, and treat confirmed bypass of weight traffic routing controls as a security event subject to investigation and session termination.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Route outbound traffic from model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference serving systems, through authenticated proxy servers at managed network boundaries. Enforce proxy authentication before permitting external connectivity from any system with access to model weights, and block direct external connections that bypass designated proxy paths. Apply content inspection at proxy egress points to detect and alert on transfers consistent with weight file exfiltration, such as large opaque binary streams to unexpected destinations. Log all proxy transactions originating from model weight environments with sufficient detail to support anomaly detection and investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy host-based boundary protection mechanisms on systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including training nodes, checkpoint storage hosts, inference servers, and workstations used for weight access. Configure these mechanisms to restrict inbound and outbound communications to those explicitly required for model weight operations, denying all other traffic by default. Extend controls to the application layer where feasible, limiting which processes and services on a given host are permitted to initiate or receive network connections involving weight data. Manage host protection configurations centrally to prevent unauthorized modification, and apply integrity monitoring to detect tampering with boundary protection settings. Ensure that host-based controls complement network-level segmentation rather than substituting for it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configure boundary protection devices for model weight networks, including firewalls, security gateways, and access control enforcement points, to fail closed, blocking all traffic rather than defaulting to an open or passthrough state on malfunction. Ensure that failure of any such device results in weight systems becoming isolated rather than exposed. Test fail-secure behavior at an organization-defined frequency to verify that failures produce the intended isolation outcome. Monitor boundary protection devices covering weight infrastructure for failure conditions and alert security operations when a device enters a degraded or failed state. Maintain documented procedures for authorized emergency access to model weight systems during security infrastructure outages, ensuring those procedures include compensating controls and post-incident review.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of model weights in transit across all transmission paths relevant to weight operations, including distributed training synchronization, checkpoint transfers between nodes, repository uploads and downloads, inference deployment pipelines, and backup or archival transfers. Enumerate the network paths over which weights travel, including internal cluster fabric, inter-datacenter links, and any paths traversing external or shared networks, and apply encryption commensurate with the sensitivity of the weights and the threat profile of each path. For weights traversing external or untrusted networks, enforce strong transport encryption and authenticate both endpoints before transmission. Verify weight integrity at transfer boundaries using cryptographic checksums or signatures, and reject or quarantine transfers that fail verification. For air-gapped or physically isolated environments, require encrypted removable media with tamper-evident controls and documented chain-of-custody procedures. Monitor transmission paths for anomalous volume, unexpected destinations, or access patterns inconsistent with authorized operations, and alert through normal security operations processes. Document authorized transmission paths and review that documentation when infrastructure changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypt all model weight data in transit between any systems involved in training, fine-tuning, checkpointing, serving, or repository storage, using strong, currently accepted cryptographic protocols and cipher suites. Apply mutual authentication for weight system communications so that both endpoints verify identity before any transfer proceeds. Enforce cryptographic integrity protection sufficient to detect unauthorized modification of weight data during transmission, and treat integrity failures as security events requiring investigation. Prohibit unencrypted transfer of model weights across any network boundary, including internal datacenter links, cross-datacenter replication paths, and connections between build pipelines and storage systems. Manage transmission encryption keys through a controlled process that prevents key exposure during weight transfer operations, and rotate keys in accordance with organizational cryptographic policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Terminate idle network connections to systems that store, serve, or process model weights at both the session and transport layers. Configure application sessions, administrative connections, and programmatic access channels to disconnect after organization-defined periods of inactivity, calibrated to the privilege level and sensitivity of the access. Require reauthentication before resuming a terminated session. Configure network infrastructure to reclaim idle TCP connections to weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference endpoints, preventing orphaned sessions from remaining exploitable. Balance timeout aggressiveness against legitimate operational needs such as long-running training jobs or checkpoint operations that require persistent connections, and document exceptions with compensating controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and manage cryptographic keys used to protect model weights throughout their full lifecycle, including generation, distribution, storage, use, and destruction. Generate keys using cryptographically secure random number generators, and store them in dedicated key management infrastructure, such as hardware security modules or cloud key management services, isolated from the weight data they protect and never embedded in source code, configuration files, or checkpoint metadata. Enforce separation between key material and encrypted weight artifacts at rest and in transit. Maintain an inventory of keys covering their purpose, associated weight assets, custodianship, and lifecycle status. Rotate keys on an organization-defined schedule based on key type, sensitivity of the protected weights, and operational risk. Establish secure key destruction procedures and apply them when weights are retired, key compromise is suspected, or custodianship changes. For the most sensitive weight assets, require multi-party authorization for key access or use, ensuring no single individual can unilaterally access protected weights without oversight. Audit key management procedures and access at an organization-defined frequency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify all cryptographic uses relevant to model weight environments, including encryption of weights at rest in repositories and checkpoint storage, encryption in transit across training clusters and serving infrastructure, integrity verification of weight artifacts, and authentication of build pipeline outputs, and implement cryptography appropriate to each use. Use authenticated encryption for weight storage and transfer to provide both confidentiality and tamper detection. Apply cryptographic integrity controls to model weight artifacts at each stage of the build and serving pipeline, enabling detection of unauthorized modification. Avoid algorithms or key lengths considered cryptographically weak by current authoritative guidance. Where regulatory or contractual requirements mandate use of validated cryptographic modules, apply those modules to weight storage and transfer operations. Maintain the ability to update cryptographic algorithms and key material across weight infrastructure without requiring full system redesign, treating cryptographic agility as an operational requirement rather than a future consideration. Document cryptographic use decisions for model weight systems and review them when threat conditions, regulatory requirements, or algorithm guidance materially change.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict remote activation of cameras, microphones, and screen-sharing capabilities on systems used to access, store, train, or serve model weights. Require explicit user-initiated confirmation before screen-sharing sessions can display weight files, training dashboards, or inference infrastructure. Provide physical or software-enforced indication when collaborative computing devices are active on workstations or terminals used in model weight environments. Disable or remove cameras and microphones from servers and storage nodes hosting model weights where no operational need exists. Apply physical controls such as privacy screens in shared or open workspaces where weight content may be visible on displays. Prohibit unauthorized photography or recording in facilities housing weight storage or training infrastructure, and communicate this restriction to all personnel and visitors. Maintain an organization-defined list of approved exceptions where remote activation is permitted, subject to compensating controls and documented justification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Issue and manage PKI certificates used to secure model weight infrastructure, including TLS certificates for weight repositories, training cluster APIs, and inference serving endpoints; client certificates for device and service authentication to weight systems; and code signing certificates used to validate weight artifacts and pipeline components. Obtain certificates from organization-approved certificate authorities, whether internal PKI or external CAs meeting organizational trust requirements. Maintain a current certificate inventory covering issuance, expiration, assigned system, and purpose for all certificates protecting weight environments. Enforce certificate validation, including expiration, revocation status, and hostname or identity matching, on all systems that store, serve, or process model weights. Rotate certificates before expiration through automated or operationally appropriate processes. Revoke certificates promptly when an associated system is decommissioned, a key is compromised, or access authorization changes. Restrict trust stores on weight infrastructure to organization-approved trust anchors and audit them periodically to detect unauthorized additions. Monitor for impending certificate expiration and alert authorized personnel with sufficient lead time to rotate without service disruption.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code technologies for systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including training pipelines, inference infrastructure, and checkpoint repositories. Authorize mobile code execution through a documented review and approval process before it is permitted to interact with weight storage or processing environments. Require integrity verification, such as cryptographic signing or hash validation, for code artifacts that access model weights, and enforce verification at execution time on production systems. Apply sandboxing or container isolation to restrict mobile code capabilities to only what is operationally required, limiting network access, filesystem scope, and privilege elevation as appropriate. Maintain allowlists of approved code artifacts or execution environments for weight-sensitive contexts, and block execution of code that fails verification or falls outside the allowlist. Monitor for unexpected or anomalous code execution in weight-adjacent environments and generate alerts consistent with operational security monitoring capability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure that DNS infrastructure supporting model weight systems, including weight repositories, training clusters, inference serving endpoints, and checkpoint storage, provides cryptographic data origin authentication and integrity verification for authoritative name resolution responses. Where DNS infrastructure operates as part of a hierarchical namespace, support chain-of-trust verification between parent and child zones so that systems resolving weight service endpoints can confirm the authenticity of responses. Restrict model weight infrastructure to organization-controlled DNS resolvers rather than public resolvers, and monitor DNS query traffic from weight systems for anomalous patterns that may indicate compromise, such as unexpected external resolution requests or high-volume subdomain queries consistent with data exfiltration. For air-gapped or network-isolated weight environments, operate local authoritative DNS without external forwarding.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce DNS security validation on all recursive and caching resolvers serving model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, inference servers, and build pipelines. Validate DNSSEC signatures where available, and reject or flag responses that fail integrity checks. Restrict recursive resolution to authorized hosts within model weight environments, denying resolution services to unauthorized systems by default. Log DNS queries from model weight infrastructure and monitor for indicators of malicious activity or data exfiltration, such as high-volume queries, unusual domain patterns, or connections to known malicious destinations. Isolate DNS resolvers serving model weight environments from general enterprise DNS infrastructure to limit lateral exposure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Architect name and address resolution services supporting model weight infrastructure, including weight repositories, training clusters, inference servers, and checkpoint storage, to be fault-tolerant and free of single points of failure. Separate internal name resolution for model weight environments from external-facing resolution, ensuring that internal weight system hostnames and service endpoints are not exposed or resolvable outside the organization's controlled network boundaries. Restrict modification of name resolution records for weight infrastructure to authorized personnel through access-controlled administrative interfaces, and log all configuration changes in a tamper-resistant audit trail integrated with security monitoring. Validate failover and resilience of name resolution for weight-critical services as part of routine infrastructure testing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions used to access, manage, or transfer model weights by using cryptographically strong session tokens that are resistant to hijacking, fixation, and replay. Regenerate session identifiers after authentication and after any privilege elevation. Invalidate sessions on logout and enforce organization-defined inactivity and maximum session lifetime limits, applying stricter limits for sessions with write or administrative access to weight repositories, training infrastructure, or serving systems. Encrypt session tokens in transit. Monitor for session anomalies relevant to model weight access, including concurrent sessions from geographically inconsistent locations, rapid session cycling, or session reuse patterns inconsistent with established user behavior, and alert through normal security operations processes. Apply additional session binding controls for privileged weight access where operationally feasible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of model weights at rest across all storage locations, including training checkpoints, weight repositories, object storage, backup systems, and archives. Apply encryption using a strong authenticated cipher at all storage tiers, with keys managed separately from the data they protect. Use envelope encryption or equivalent key hierarchy practices so that data keys encrypting weights are themselves protected by key encryption keys under centralized key management. Store and manage keys using hardware or software key management infrastructure with access controls, audit logging, and rotation practices appropriate to the sensitivity of the weights. Monitor storage environments for unencrypted weight files and generate alerts on detection. Verify encryption coverage periodically through configuration review or equivalent testing to confirm that newly provisioned storage locations and backup destinations conform to policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypt model weights and associated artifacts at rest across all environments where they are stored or processed, including weight repositories, checkpoint storage, training cluster scratch space, and inference serving infrastructure. Apply encryption to weight files, checkpoint files, serialized tensors, gradient checkpoints, and optimizer states. Use envelope encryption so that data encryption keys protect the weight artifacts directly and key encryption keys protect those data encryption keys, with key material stored in a hardware-backed key management system or equivalent service that enforces access controls and audit logging over key operations. Apply full-disk or volume-level encryption on systems that store or process model weights as a complementary layer. Rotate encryption keys at an organization-defined frequency informed by risk, ensuring that key rotation procedures are tested and do not create availability gaps in training or serving workflows. Restrict key management access to authorized personnel and log all key lifecycle operations, including creation, rotation, access, and deletion, through the organization's security monitoring capability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Partition model weight infrastructure into separate physical or logical domains based on function, sensitivity, and risk. At minimum, isolate training and fine-tuning infrastructure from inference and serving infrastructure, and separate development and staging environments from production weight systems. Maintain production weight storage in fully internal network segments, placing any externally accessible weight-serving APIs in isolated boundary zones with no direct access to backend weight repositories. Apply distinct authentication domains, network controls, and storage boundaries across partitions so that a compromise of one environment cannot directly propagate to another. Document partition boundaries, enforce them through technical controls such as network segmentation and separate credential stores, and verify that enforcement remains effective after significant infrastructure changes or security incidents.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Isolate privileged functions protecting model weights, including key management, access control enforcement, and weight encryption operations, onto physically separate infrastructure from general-purpose compute, training workloads, and inference serving systems. Use dedicated hardware or hardware security modules for cryptographic operations over model weights, and physically separate systems hosting those functions from untrusted or shared-tenant environments. Prohibit co-location of privileged weight protection functions with workloads that do not require equivalent access controls, and document the physical separation boundaries as part of the model weight security architecture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce process isolation for workloads that load, serve, train, or otherwise process model weights, ensuring that weight-handling processes cannot be read, modified, or interrupted by unauthorized processes on the same host. Apply operating system-level mandatory access controls or equivalent enforcement mechanisms to restrict inter-process communication and memory access between weight-handling processes and unrelated workloads. Run weight-serving and weight-processing workloads in isolated execution environments, such as containers or virtual machines, configured with resource boundaries and minimal capability sets. Prohibit debugging, memory inspection, or attachment to weight-handling processes except by authorized personnel acting under an approved process with appropriate logging. Monitor for process injection attempts, unexpected inter-process access, or anomalous memory access patterns targeting weight-handling workloads. Where the underlying hardware platform supports confidential computing features, evaluate their use for weight-processing workloads based on threat exposure and operational feasibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Synchronize system clocks across all infrastructure that stores, trains, serves, or processes model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, inference servers, build pipelines, and security monitoring systems, using authoritative time sources appropriate to the environment. Maintain time consistency at a precision sufficient to enable accurate correlation of security events across these systems. Monitor for time synchronization failures and alert authorized personnel. Log synchronization status and detect anomalous clock drift or manipulation attempts, as time skew or tampering may obscure the sequence of events during a security incident involving model weight access or exfiltration. Use authenticated time synchronization protocols where the infrastructure supports them, and maintain backup time sources to ensure continuity if a primary source becomes unavailable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Synchronize clocks across all systems involved in model weight storage, training, serving, and audit logging with an authoritative time source using authenticated time synchronization protocols that resist spoofing or manipulation. Maintain sufficient clock accuracy across weight infrastructure to support reliable correlation of security events, such as unauthorized access attempts, checkpoint exfiltration, or pipeline anomalies, across training clusters, weight repositories, and inference servers. Alert when a system loses synchronization or diverges beyond an organization-defined threshold, as clock skew or failure may indicate tampering, misconfiguration, or an attempt to disrupt audit trail integrity. Protect time synchronization infrastructure with access controls consistent with other critical model weight security services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and periodically update system integrity policy and procedures covering the infrastructure used to store, train, fine-tune, and serve model weights. Policy must address purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across relevant environments including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Procedures must support consistent implementation of integrity controls across those environments, including cryptographic verification of weight files, monitoring for anomalous access or modification, and response to integrity failures. Designate organization-defined personnel or roles to own the development, maintenance, and dissemination of this policy. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant changes to model weight infrastructure, threat landscape, or organizational risk posture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify, report, and remediate flaws in systems that store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights, including weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference servers. Prioritize remediation based on risk to model weight confidentiality and integrity, applying faster timelines to vulnerabilities affecting direct weight access paths, privileged interfaces, or cryptographic protections than to lower-risk supporting systems. Test software and firmware updates in a representative environment before applying them to production weight infrastructure, with particular attention to side effects on training stability, serving performance, or weight integrity verification. When a flaw cannot be remediated promptly, implement documented compensating controls, such as network segmentation, enhanced monitoring, or access restriction, and track outstanding flaws through a risk acceptance process with organization-defined review cycles. For container-based weight serving or training environments, establish a process to rebuild and redeploy images when base image vulnerabilities materially increase risk to model weights. Incorporate flaw remediation into the configuration management process governing model weight infrastructure so that patching is tracked, auditable, and does not introduce unauthorized changes to weight-adjacent systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use automated mechanisms to assess patch and update status across infrastructure that stores, trains, fine-tunes, or serves model weights, including training clusters, weight repositories, inference servers, and checkpoint storage. Scan at an organization-defined frequency sufficient to detect unpatched components before they can be exploited, and generate alerts when systems fall outside the organization's defined patch baseline. Integrate status checks into build and deployment pipelines so that components with known unresolved vulnerabilities are flagged before gaining access to model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Measure the time between flaw identification and remediation for systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, and inference infrastructure. Establish organization-defined remediation benchmarks tiered by severity, with tighter timelines for vulnerabilities that are actively exploited or that directly affect weight access controls, encryption, or authentication. Track and review remediation metrics at an organization-defined frequency to identify systemic delays or chronically unpatched systems. Document and approve exceptions through a defined risk acceptance process, with compensating controls applied for the duration of any approved deferral.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy automated patch management tooling across model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, inference servers, checkpoint storage systems, and build pipelines, to detect, assess, and apply approved patches without requiring manual intervention for each update cycle. Prioritize remediation of vulnerabilities in components directly involved in weight storage, access control, and data movement. Test patches in a representative staging environment before automated rollout to production weight systems, and generate alerts for components that fall outside approved patch compliance windows so that exceptions are tracked and resolved through a documented process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enable automatic installation of security-relevant updates for operating system components, ML framework dependencies, and firmware on infrastructure that stores, trains, or serves model weights. Scope automatic updates to security-critical components where the risk of unpatched vulnerabilities exceeds the risk of update-induced instability; for weight-serving or training systems where uncontrolled updates could disrupt availability or integrity, require updates to pass through a defined staging or validation step before production deployment. Maintain a documented set of systems or components excluded from automatic updates, subject these exclusions to periodic review, and ensure excluded systems receive compensating controls or expedited manual patching.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: After installing updated versions of software components that store, process, or serve model weights, including ML frameworks, checkpoint management tools, weight serialization libraries, and inference runtimes, remove the previous versions from training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, and serving infrastructure. Maintain a current inventory of software versions present on these systems, and remediate or document justified exceptions for any retained legacy versions where removal would disrupt active workflows. Where legacy versions are temporarily retained, apply compensating controls and schedule removal with organization-defined urgency proportionate to the vulnerability risk they present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy malicious code protection across systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, weight repositories, and inference servers. Apply protection at entry and exit points where model weights, training data, framework packages, and pipeline artifacts are introduced, transferred, or executed. Keep detection mechanisms current through automated updates aligned with the organization's configuration management practices. Configure periodic scans of model weight infrastructure and real-time scanning of externally sourced files, including ML framework downloads, dependency packages, and weight files received from third parties, at the point of download, open, or execution. On detection, block or quarantine malicious code and alert organization-defined personnel through operational security channels. Account for false positives in scanning configurations, particularly for large binary checkpoint files and compiled kernels that may trigger heuristic detections, and establish a process to resolve false positives without unnecessarily disrupting training runs or weight serving availability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitor systems that store, train, fine-tune, and serve model weights to detect attacks, unauthorized access, anomalous behavior, and indicators of potential exfiltration or tampering. Deploy monitoring coverage across weight repositories, training clusters, build pipelines, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure, positioning collection at network boundaries, storage access layers, and within compute environments. Establish detection logic tuned to model weight environments, including unusual bulk reads or transfers of weight files, unexpected access to checkpoint directories, privilege escalations on training or serving infrastructure, anomalous API call patterns against model serving endpoints, and access originating from unexpected locations or accounts. Monitor for insider threat indicators such as atypical access volume, access outside normal working patterns, or access sequences that deviate from established role behavior. Correlate events across infrastructure layers, storage, network, identity, and compute, to detect multi-stage attacks that would not be visible from any single layer alone. Analyze detected events and anomalies to distinguish genuine threats from noise, and route alerts to security operations through established processes. Adjust monitoring depth and coverage in response to changes in risk posture, such as active incidents, personnel changes, or new attack intelligence. Obtain legal review of monitoring activities to ensure they are consistent with applicable law and organizational policy. Provide monitoring findings and summaries to organization-defined roles on a frequency and in a format appropriate to operational needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Integrate monitoring signals from model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, weight repositories, build pipelines, inference servers, and checkpoint storage, into a unified detection capability that correlates events across sources. Ensure that alerts from network monitoring, host-based detection, access control systems, and data movement controls are visible together, enabling detection of multi-stage attack patterns such as privilege escalation followed by weight access and bulk exfiltration. Configure correlation logic to identify distributed or low-and-slow attacks that would not trigger alerts when viewed in isolation on any single system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy automated monitoring tools that perform continuous analysis of events across model weight repositories, training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving infrastructure. Ensure detection operates with low enough latency to support timely investigation and response to suspicious activity, such as unauthorized access attempts, unusual bulk reads or transfers, privilege escalations, or unexpected access to high-value weights. Integrate detection outputs into security operations workflows so that alerts reach appropriate personnel through established channels without requiring manual log review as the primary means of detection. Configure automated tooling to cover the access patterns most relevant to model weight theft or exfiltration by insider or external threat actors, and tune detection to reduce alert fatigue while maintaining meaningful coverage of high-risk behaviors.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic for model weight environments continuously or at an organization-defined frequency, using criteria calibrated to exfiltration and infiltration risks specific to weight storage, training, and serving infrastructure. Establish traffic baselines for systems that store, transfer, or serve model weights, and alert on deviations such as anomalous outbound transfer volumes, connections to unexpected external destinations, unusual use of encrypted tunnels or non-standard protocols, and bulk transfers occurring outside normal operational patterns. Monitor inference serving endpoints for traffic patterns consistent with model extraction, including high-volume or systematically structured query flows that suggest probing of model behavior or outputs at scale. Apply outbound inspection appropriate to the sensitivity of weights in scope, sufficient to detect weight file signatures or large structured payloads leaving the environment through unexpected channels. Tune detection criteria to reduce alert fatigue while maintaining meaningful coverage of the threat vectors most relevant to organized, capable adversaries targeting model weights.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Generate and route alerts to organization-defined security personnel when monitoring systems detect indicators of potential model weight compromise, including anomalous access patterns to weight repositories, bulk or unexpected weight file transfers, integrity verification failures, unusual encryption key access events, unauthorized attempts to access or modify weights, and privileged operations on weight infrastructure that deviate from established baselines. Tune alert thresholds and routing to reflect the operational characteristics of training clusters, checkpoint storage, and inference serving environments, distinguishing genuine anomalies from expected high-volume or automated activity. Ensure alerts include sufficient context, such as the account, system, operation, and recent activity sequence, to support timely triage and response without requiring manual correlation of disparate log sources.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Correlate security event data across model weight infrastructure, including authentication systems, access logs for weight repositories and serving endpoints, network telemetry, and data movement alerts, to detect attack patterns that span multiple systems or unfold gradually over time. Implement correlation logic capable of linking related events such as credential activity followed by weight access followed by unusual data transfer, and of identifying cumulative low-volume access patterns that individually appear benign but collectively indicate unauthorized weight extraction. Centralize or federate correlated event data in a manner accessible to security operations, and ensure correlation outputs are structured to support incident investigation and attack timeline reconstruction.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Analyze outbound communications from model weight infrastructure at external boundaries and at organization-defined interior points, including training clusters, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and inference servers, to detect covert exfiltration of model weights or related artifacts. Monitor for low-and-slow transfer patterns, protocol abuse such as DNS or ICMP tunneling, and encoding techniques that may conceal weight data within otherwise legitimate traffic. At inference boundaries, detect query patterns consistent with model extraction attempts, including systematic input space exploration, gradient estimation probes, and high-volume repetitive querying that deviates from expected usage profiles. Correlate anomalies across network, access, and query logs to distinguish extraction activity from legitimate research or operational workloads, and route alerts to security operations for investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy host-based monitoring on systems that store, process, serve, or transfer model weights. Monitor for process execution anomalies, unauthorized access to weight files or checkpoint directories, unusual memory access patterns associated with weight loading or extraction, privilege escalation attempts, and lateral movement from weight-adjacent systems. Apply file integrity monitoring to weight repositories and checkpoint storage, alerting on unexpected modifications, deletions, or bulk reads. Protect host-based monitoring agents against tampering by users with local administrative access, ensuring monitoring continuity is not contingent on the cooperation of the monitored account. Forward host-based telemetry to centralized logging infrastructure where it can be correlated with access logs, network activity, and authentication events.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain a process for receiving, evaluating, and acting on security alerts, advisories, and vulnerability disclosures relevant to model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage systems, weight repositories, inference serving platforms, and the frameworks and dependencies used to load and execute weights. Subscribe to threat intelligence and vulnerability feeds covering the software and hardware components of model weight environments, and monitor for emerging exploitation techniques targeting AI workloads, including attacks on serialization formats, model serving APIs, and distributed training communication layers. Generate internal advisories when newly identified vulnerabilities or threat intelligence have material relevance to model weight storage, access, or integrity. Disseminate alerts to organization-defined personnel responsible for securing, operating, or maintaining model weight environments in a timely manner, prioritizing based on exploitability and potential impact. Track remediation of actionable advisories to closure, escalate items where remediation is delayed beyond organization-defined thresholds, and maintain records sufficient to demonstrate that relevant alerts were assessed and dispositioned.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Verify that security functions protecting model weight environments operate correctly, including access controls on weight repositories, encryption of weights at rest and in transit, audit logging pipelines, authentication enforcement for weight system access, and anomaly detection covering training clusters, inference infrastructure, and checkpoint storage. Perform verification at organization-defined frequencies and upon significant system changes, such as infrastructure updates, pipeline modifications, or deployment of new weight serving configurations. Alert organization-defined personnel or roles when verification tests fail or produce anomalous results, and take organization-defined response actions, such as isolating affected systems, suspending weight access, or initiating incident response, proportionate to the nature and severity of the failure. Treat repeated or correlated verification failures as potential indicators of active compromise or misconfiguration requiring investigation, not routine operational noise.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain cryptographic integrity verification for model weights across all stages of the weight lifecycle, including initial generation, checkpoint storage, repository commits, build pipeline outputs, and inference loading. Generate and store authoritative hash values for all production and candidate weight files in tamper-evident, access-controlled storage that is separate from the weight files themselves. Sign approved model weights using HSM-backed or equivalent cryptographically protected key material, with signing key access logged and restricted to authorized personnel or automated pipeline roles. Verify weight integrity at each lifecycle transition, prior to inference loading, on export or transfer, and after any pipeline step that reads or writes weights, by comparing against trusted reference values. Require signed commits from authorized personnel in model weight repositories and flag or block unsigned or unverified commits through pipeline enforcement controls. Implement platform integrity controls, such as secure boot or equivalent verified launch mechanisms, on infrastructure that stores or serves model weights. Define and document organizational responses to failed integrity checks, including alert generation, automatic blocking of affected weight versions from serving, escalation to security operations, and investigation procedures. Treat integrity failures as potential security incidents and retain associated logs under controls that prevent modification or deletion.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Perform integrity verification on model weights and the software used to load, serve, and manage them at security-relevant points: at system or service startup, before weights are loaded into inference or training processes, and when weights transition between environments such as from checkpoint storage to a serving system or from training infrastructure to a repository. Generate and store cryptographic manifests for weight artifacts during training or fine-tuning and verify them at each subsequent transition or deployment. Apply integrity checks to the ML framework and weight-serving software at startup to detect unauthorized modifications before weights are processed. Trigger additional integrity checks on anomalous events such as unexpected weight file changes, failed access attempts, or alerts from storage-layer monitoring. Protect manifests and integrity records with access controls separate from the weight artifacts themselves so that an attacker who modifies weights cannot silently update the corresponding hashes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configure automated integrity verification systems to generate alerts when discrepancies are detected in model weights, checkpoints, or related artifacts across training, storage, and serving environments. Route alerts to organization-defined personnel or roles with sufficient context to support investigation, including identification of the affected artifact, the nature of the discrepancy, and relevant access or pipeline activity preceding the event. Integrate alerting with operational security monitoring processes so that integrity violations receive timely triage consistent with organizational incident response procedures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Manage integrity verification tools for model weight infrastructure from a centralized, hardened management plane that is administratively and logically separated from the weight storage, training, and serving systems it monitors. Ensure that integrity baselines for model weights, checkpoints, and associated configuration are maintained centrally, that verification results are aggregated and reviewable across all weight infrastructure, and that policy governing what is verified and how frequently is applied consistently rather than configured locally on individual systems. Protect the management plane and its baseline records from modification by the systems being monitored.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Integrate model weight integrity violations, including unexpected weight modifications, failed cryptographic verification, unauthorized checkpoint alterations, and anomalous changes to model artifacts in repositories, training clusters, or serving infrastructure, into the organizational incident response capability. Automatically escalate integrity failures to incident response workflows, ensuring that alerts from weight integrity monitoring are not silently discarded or left unresolved. Maintain documented response procedures covering common weight integrity scenarios, including corrupted checkpoints, unauthorized fine-tuning, and suspected exfiltration via weight modification. Periodically exercise response procedures to verify that integrity alerts are actionable, correctly routed, and that response personnel understand the operational impact of weight integrity events in training and serving environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Verify the integrity of the boot process for systems that store, process, or serve model weights using platform-appropriate mechanisms such as measured boot, cryptographic image verification, or remote attestation. Require successful boot integrity verification before granting access to model weights, and block startup or deny weight access when verification fails. Monitor boot integrity records to detect unauthorized modifications to firmware, bootloaders, or base system images. Where the environment supports it, use remote attestation to enable centralized verification of weight-serving infrastructure boot state before permitting network access to weight storage or serving endpoints.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy spam and phishing protection at email and messaging entry points for personnel with access to model weight systems, with particular attention to credential phishing, social engineering targeting weight access credentials, and impersonation of internal ML infrastructure services or trusted external providers. Keep filtering mechanisms current as part of standard configuration management practices. Supplement technical controls with periodic awareness activities that help authorized personnel recognize and report suspicious messages related to model weight access or AI infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automatically update spam and phishing protection mechanisms for systems and personnel involved in model weight operations, including email gateways, web proxies, and endpoint protection tools. Ensure updates occur at an organization-defined frequency sufficient to address current threats, with minimal manual intervention required. Apply protections to users with access to weight repositories, training infrastructure, and serving systems, where targeted phishing and social engineering campaigns represent a realistic path to credential theft or unauthorized weight access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Validate all inputs at interfaces that handle model weight artifacts, training data, and configuration parameters before processing or storage. For weight and checkpoint files, verify format integrity, including structural validity and expected file signatures, prior to loading into training, fine-tuning, or serving infrastructure. Validate training data uploads for expected type, structure, and content constraints before ingestion into pipelines. Enforce input constraints on model weight access APIs, including request structure, parameter ranges, and authentication tokens, rejecting malformed or out-of-bounds inputs at the boundary. Log input validation failures with sufficient attribution, source, interface, and input type, to support detection of probing or injection attempts targeting weight storage or serving systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish a manual override capability for input validation on interfaces that accept data into model weight serving, fine-tuning, and training pipelines, including inference APIs and weight update submission paths. Restrict use of this override to organization-defined authorized personnel, require documented justification for each invocation, and apply dual approval for overrides affecting weight modification or fine-tuning inputs. Log all override use with sufficient detail to identify who invoked the override, what validation was bypassed, and what input was submitted. Monitor overridden inputs for indicators of adversarial payloads, including prompt injection attempts or inputs designed to corrupt model behavior or checkpoint integrity. Review override usage at an organization-defined frequency to identify patterns that may indicate misuse or abuse of the capability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish a process to review and resolve input validation errors on model weight inference and serving systems within an organization-defined period. Investigate recurring or patterned validation failures that may indicate adversarial probing, prompt injection attempts, or model extraction queries. Use error analysis to update validation rules and detection logic, and document resolutions that require changes to input handling. Track validation error trends over time to detect shifts that may signal coordinated attack activity against inference endpoints.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure that systems serving, fine-tuning, or otherwise processing model weights behave in documented, predictable ways when receiving malformed, unexpected, or adversarial inputs. Define and document expected system behavior for invalid or boundary-case inputs across inference APIs, fine-tuning pipelines, and checkpoint loading routines, and verify that actual behavior matches those definitions. Apply input validation at ingestion points for fine-tuning data to reject structurally malformed payloads before they reach training or weight-update processes. For inference-serving systems, validate that responses to invalid or adversarial inputs do not expose weight values, architecture details, or internal system state beyond what is operationally required. Monitor serving and pipeline systems for patterns consistent with systematic boundary probing or repeated malformed inputs that may indicate an adversary mapping input validation behavior as a precursor to exploitation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Account for timing interactions among components that store, process, or serve model weights when designing responses to invalid or anomalous inputs.
