Ensure that validation logic for weight-serving APIs, checkpoint access operations, and inference pipelines does not introduce timing differentials that leak information about internal state, access control decisions, or cryptographic operations. Use constant-time comparisons for authentication and authorization checks on weight access paths. Monitor inference and access API latency patterns for systematic anomalies that may indicate timing-based probing, and apply rate limiting to weight-serving endpoints to constrain the ability of adversaries to collect high-resolution timing measurements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict inputs to model weight training, fine-tuning, and inference pipelines to organization-defined trusted sources and approved formats. Maintain a registry of approved data sources for training and fine-tuning, and require documented authorization before introducing external datasets or checkpoints. Enforce format allow-lists at ingestion boundaries, for example, rejecting serialization formats known to permit arbitrary code execution in favor of safer alternatives, and validate that uploaded or transferred weight files conform to expected structure before loading. Scan weight checkpoints and training data ingested from external or lower-trust sources for signs of malicious content or tampering prior to use. Apply input validation at inference API endpoints to reject inputs that fall outside approved formats, types, or bounds, reducing the attack surface for prompt injection or serialization-based exploitation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce input validation and injection prevention across all interfaces that accept untrusted data into model weight infrastructure, including inference endpoints, weight management systems, training job submission pipelines, and checkpoint storage APIs. Validate and sanitize inputs at trust boundaries before they reach weight processing logic, query execution layers, or orchestration scripts. Apply output filtering at inference endpoints to limit responses that could facilitate systematic model extraction or weight reconstruction through repeated or crafted queries. Monitor inference traffic and pipeline inputs for patterns consistent with injection attempts, model extraction probes, or membership inference queries, and adjust defenses as attack patterns evolve.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configure model weight serving systems, training infrastructure, APIs, and build pipelines to return generic error messages to external callers and end users while routing detailed diagnostic information, including stack traces, internal paths, and system state, exclusively to secure, access-controlled logging infrastructure. Ensure error output does not expose model weight storage locations, checkpoint paths, architecture details, training metadata, or underlying infrastructure configuration. Restrict detailed error output to authorized personnel with a legitimate operational need, and periodically review error handling logic in weight-serving and training pipeline code to confirm sensitive information is not inadvertently surfaced through error responses.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose:
Establish and maintain information lifecycle policies for model weights that define retention requirements, secure deletion procedures, and version control practices across all weight environments, including training checkpoints, experimental runs, fine-tuned variants, production-serving weights, and offline archives. Align retention periods and archival schedules to operational need and organizational risk tolerance rather than fixed durations, and review them periodically as model usage and business requirements evolve.

Require that all copies of model weights, across repositories, training clusters, inference infrastructure, backup systems, and any offline or cold storage, be tracked in an asset inventory sufficient to support deletion, audit, and incident response. Ensure that deletion of model weights uses methods appropriate to the sensitivity of the weights and the storage medium, such as cryptographic erasure for encrypted storage or verified overwrite for other media, and confirm deletion through the inventory record.

Apply version control to production and near-production model weights, with access logging sufficient to reconstruct who accessed or modified which version and when. For training checkpoints and experimental weights, establish policies governing how long intermediate artifacts are retained and when they are purged, prioritizing consistent automated enforcement over manual processes. Require explicit authorization and documented justification for retaining weights beyond their standard policy period, and treat unjustified accumulation of copies as a risk indicator warranting review.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dispose of model weights, checkpoints, and associated metadata using techniques appropriate to the storage medium and sensitivity of the weights. For software-based deletion on standard storage, apply cryptographic erasure by destroying or rotating encryption keys to render weights unrecoverable, or apply multi-pass overwriting where cryptographic erasure is not available. For physical media that stored model weights, apply physical destruction or degaussing through documented processes. For cloud-stored weights, treat key destruction as the primary disposal mechanism and confirm that no recoverable copies remain in backup, replication, or snapshot systems. Document disposal actions for each weight artifact, including what was disposed of, when, by what method, and by whom. Periodically verify that disposal processes are functioning as intended through spot-checks or technical validation appropriate to the environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enable OS-level memory protections on all systems that store, process, or serve model weights, including execute-disable enforcement, address space layout randomization, and stack protection mechanisms. Ensure that ML frameworks and runtime environments used for training, fine-tuning, and inference are built or configured with equivalent protections enabled. Clear model weights and intermediate activation data from CPU and GPU memory after inference sessions, checkpoint operations, or other processing tasks complete, using memory management practices appropriate to the frameworks and accelerators in use. Run inference and training processes with minimal privileges and enforce memory isolation between workloads, using containerization or equivalent mechanisms to prevent cross-process memory access. Monitor systems hosting model weights for suspicious memory access patterns, including unauthorized debugger attachment, memory scanning activity, and anomalous access to process memory interfaces, and generate alerts through normal security operations channels. Apply organization-defined additional memory protections, such as hardware-based memory encryption for inference enclaves, where the sensitivity of the model weights and the assessed threat level justify the operational and performance tradeoffs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop, document, and maintain supply chain risk management policy and procedures scoped to the acquisition, development, and operational dependencies of model weight infrastructure. Address the full supply chain surface relevant to model weights, including training hardware and firmware, model weight repositories and artifact registries, third-party base models and pretrained weights, inference serving software, and cloud or colocation providers hosting weight storage and training clusters. Policy must define purpose, scope, responsibilities, management commitment, and coordination across teams involved in procuring or operating model weight infrastructure. Procedures must operationalize the policy, covering how supply chain risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated across the weight lifecycle from acquisition through deployment and retirement. Disseminate policy and procedures to organization-defined personnel or roles responsible for procurement, infrastructure, security, and model operations. Designate an organization-defined official accountable for maintaining and updating these materials. Review and update policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following significant supply chain events such as discovery of a compromised dependency, a major third-party breach affecting model weight tooling, or a material change in the organization's model weight supply chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Develop and maintain a supply chain risk management plan that addresses risks associated with the acquisition, integration, operation, and disposal of components and services used in model weight environments, including training frameworks and libraries, data pipeline tooling, orchestration and scheduling platforms, weight storage systems, inference runtimes, and third-party model components. The plan should document the organization's tolerance for supply chain risk as it relates to model weight security, identify the highest-priority supply chain risks to weight confidentiality and integrity, and describe the controls and processes in place to manage those risks across the system lifecycle. Include processes for evaluating supply chain risk before acquiring new components or services that will have access to model weights, and for reassessing risk when the supply chain environment changes materially. Establish roles and responsibilities for supply chain risk management activities, including who is responsible for supplier vetting, component integrity verification, and monitoring for supply chain compromise indicators. Review and update the plan at an organization-defined frequency and in response to significant changes in the threat environment, organizational supply chain relationships, or findings from security assessments. Protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification, as its contents may reveal exploitable details about the organization's supply chain dependencies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain supply chain risk management processes covering components and services used to store, train, fine-tune, or serve model weights, including training frameworks, checkpoint storage systems, orchestration platforms, inference runtimes, and third-party data pipelines. Identify and assess supply chain weaknesses before procurement and at organization-defined intervals thereafter, prioritizing components with privileged access to weight files, cryptographic material, or training infrastructure. Require suppliers of high-risk components to meet organization-defined security requirements, including vulnerability disclosure processes and incident notification obligations. Maintain a component inventory covering third-party software and services integrated into model weight pipelines, sufficient to support rapid identification and response when a supply chain compromise is suspected. Apply integrity verification to third-party components before integration into weight training or serving environments, and restrict the use of unvetted or unsigned artifacts in production pipelines. Document implemented supply chain controls, findings from supplier assessments, and any accepted risks in a maintained record appropriate to the organization's risk management processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain acquisition strategies for software, hardware, and services used in model weight infrastructure, including ML frameworks, training libraries, accelerator drivers, and inference runtimes, that explicitly address supply chain risk. Require procurement processes to evaluate vendor security posture, including secure development practices, vulnerability disclosure programs, and patch responsiveness, before acquisition decisions are finalized. Obtain packages and dependencies from official, authoritative sources and verify integrity through signatures or checksums prior to installation in any environment that stores, trains, or serves model weights. Maintain a documented inventory of critical suppliers and dependencies with associated risk assessments, and review that inventory at an organization-defined frequency. Monitor for supply chain compromises affecting components in active use, and establish a process for responding when a trusted dependency or vendor is found to be compromised. Where feasible, avoid single-supplier dependencies for components critical to model weight security, integrity, or availability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain notification agreements with vendors, suppliers, and service providers whose software, hardware, or services are involved in storing, training, fine-tuning, or serving model weights. These agreements must require counterparties to notify the organization of security incidents, discovered vulnerabilities, or supply chain compromises that could affect the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of model weights or the infrastructure that protects them. Include notification requirements in procurement contracts and service agreements, covering the scope of reportable events and expectations around timeliness. Designate organization-defined contact points for receiving and routing vendor notifications. Integrate incoming notifications into existing vulnerability management and incident response processes so that reported issues affecting model weight environments are assessed, prioritized, and acted upon. Periodically verify that notification channels are functional and that responsible personnel can receive and act on alerts from vendors without delay.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Inspect systems and components used in model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, checkpoint storage, inference servers, weight repositories, and build pipeline nodes, to detect tampering, counterfeit hardware, or unauthorized software modifications. Conduct inspections upon receipt of new hardware, before deployment into production weight environments, and at an organization-defined frequency for deployed systems. For hardware, verify that physical tamper indicators are intact, that components match procurement records, and that no unexpected devices or modifications are present. For software and firmware, verify cryptographic signatures and checksums against authoritative source values before installation or update. Quarantine any component that fails inspection or presents anomalous indicators, and investigate before allowing it into contact with model weight infrastructure. Prioritize inspection rigor based on the component's access to weights and its position in the trust chain, components with direct read or write access to model weights or their protection mechanisms warrant the most thorough review. Document inspection outcomes and retain records sufficient to support incident investigation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and maintain component authenticity verification practices for hardware and software components used in model weight infrastructure, including training clusters, inference servers, weight repositories, checkpoint storage, and build pipelines. Procure hardware components through verified manufacturers or authorized distribution channels, and validate hardware authenticity using manufacturer-provided mechanisms such as serial number verification, signed firmware, or hardware attestation features where available. For software dependencies used in weight training, fine-tuning, and serving workflows, including ML frameworks, numerical libraries, and container base images, verify cryptographic signatures or checksums against authoritative sources before deployment. Maintain an inventory of components used in model weight infrastructure that includes authenticity verification records. When a component is suspected to be counterfeit or tampered with, remove it from service, initiate an investigation, and report the finding to the component source and to organization-defined internal and external parties as appropriate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain configuration control over hardware and software components in model weight infrastructure that are awaiting service, repair, or return to service. Before removing components, including storage media, accelerators, or networking hardware, from systems that store, process, or serve model weights, record the component's identity, configuration state, and any sensitive data it may retain. Apply physical controls to removed components during the service period to prevent unauthorized access, tampering, or substitution. Before returning serviced or repaired components to production, verify component integrity and authenticity, confirm that configuration state is consistent with pre-service records or intended baseline, and ensure that any weight data or cryptographic material that may have been accessible has been accounted for or purged in accordance with organizational data handling requirements. Apply equivalent controls to software components, such as ML framework dependencies, serving runtimes, or pipeline tooling, that are taken out of service for patching or update and subsequently reintroduced into the model weight environment.
